articles.summary: Equipe de jornalismo faz cobertura especial da votação nas principais cidades da região neste domingo.
articles.body:
Equipe de jornalismo faz cobertura especial da votação nas principais cidades da região neste domingo.

Votação avança sem formação de filas nas seções do Colégio Estadual Canadá, no bairro Olaria, em Nova Friburgo, na manhã deste domingo (25).

No Colégio Estadual Canadá, no bairro Olaria, a movimentação é tranquila neste período da manhã. Este é o local de votação com o maior número de pessoas aptas a votar em Nova Friburgo. A expectativa é que mais de seis mil pessoas passem neste ponto ao longo do dia.

Senhor de 91 anos é aplaudido após votar em Petrópolis

José de Almeida, de 91 anos, é Português e não deixa de exercer o direito ao voto. Ele votou acompanhado da família, na manhã deste domingo (25), no Colégio Estadual Dom Pedro II, centro de Petrópolis.

Após concluir o voto, José foi aplaudido pela família e mesários que estavam presentes na seção.

Votação tranquila nos dois maiores locais de votação da 29ª Zona Eleitoral de Petrópolis.

Desde as 8h, quando os portões foram abertos, os eleitores têm conseguido votar com tranquilidade na Universidade Católica de Petrópolis (UCP), onde votam 5.098 eleitores e no Colégio Estadual Dom Pedro II, que reúne 5.077 eleitores.

A maioria das seções está sem filas até o momento, e a votação ocorre de forma rápida.

Até agora, nenhuma ocorrência foi registrada em Petrópolis.

Dona Marly Rodrigues Xavier, de 87 anos, acordou cedo e foi exercer a cidadania. Mesmo liberada da obrigatoriedade do voto, fez questão de ir votar na Universidade Católica de Petrópolis (UCP). Segundo ela, a votação foi rápida e tranquila.

Colégio municipal Prisco de Almeida, no Parque Calabouço, sm Campos com manhã de votação tranquila. Neste ponto de votação no primeiro turno teve uma grande movimentação.

Eleitores já começam a chegar nos locais de votação em Petrópolis, na Região Serrana do Rio. O dia começou com chuva, mas nada que impeça o cidadão de exercer o direito ao voto.

Uma fila já começou a ser formada em frente à Universidade Católica de Petrópolis (UCP), onde votam 5098 eleitores.

articles.title: The narrative battle over France’s unrest
articles.summary: Student protests, police violence and French media obsessed with ‘barbarians’.
articles.body:
What began as protests over education has rapidly taken over the streets of France and turned into one of the country’s biggest waves of unrest in years.

Many mainstream media outlets have focused their coverage on the violence and looting rather than on the demands of the demonstrators. A lot of airtime has fixated on who the protesters are and what they look like, often using racist terms. That narrative has been picked up by right-wing movements abroad.

Contributors: Cole Stangler – author, Paris Is Not Dead, and lecturer, American College of the Mediterranean Diane de Vignemont – Paris-based journalist Harrison Stetler – lecturer and writer Philippe Marliere – professor of French and European politics, University College London

Israel’s elections are just days away and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has reverted to a familiar alarmist tactic to consolidate support: hyping an “imminent” threat from Iran and telling the United States that it should “finish the job”. Meenakshi Ravi looks at the messaging.

Olga Rudenko: Independent journalism is the ‘ultimate patriotic act’

More than four and a half years into Russia’s full-scale invasion, Ukraine remains under attack, and its journalists are forced to balance many responsibilities at once.

They are documenting a war that has become more dangerous than ever, countering Russian propaganda efforts and trying to hold their own government to account at a time when the news media have been expected to fall into line. The Kyiv Independent, an online newspaper, has been doing all three since 2021.

The Listening Post spoke with its editor-in-chief and cofounder Olga Rudenko about the pressures of reporting when your country is at war.

articles.title: Chuvas em MG causam falta de energia para 636 mil clientes, diz Cemig | G1
articles.standfirst: Só na Grande BH foram 380 mil afetados, o que representa 4% do total; 221 mil imóveis estão na capital mineira. Temporal deixou 349 locais de votação sem luz no estado.
articles.summary: Só na Grande BH foram 380 mil afetados, o que representa 4% do total; 221 mil imóveis estão na capital mineira. Temporal deixou 349 locais de votação sem luz no estado.
articles.body:
As fortes chuvas que atingiram o estado na tarde deste domingo (25) , quando ocorre o segundo turno da eleição presidencial, provocaram a queda de energia para 636 mil clientes da Companhia Energética de Minas Gerais (Cemig). O número equivale a 6,6% do total de imóveis, segundo a empresa.

Só na Região Metropolitana de Belo Horizonte, foram 380 mil afetados, ou 4% do total — desse valor, 221 mil clientes estão na capital mineira, onde o temporal alagou ruas, destelhou casas, derrubou árvores e deixou sem luz 44 locais de votação .

Em BH, até a última atualização desta reportagem, um homem estava sendo procurado após, segundo os bombeiros, ser levado pela água em um córrego, e um motociclista foi atendido com parada cardiorrespiratória depois ser eletrocutado ao ser atingido por um cabo de alta tensão.

Conforme a Cemig, Minas Gerais registrou rajadas de vento de até 150 km/h em Patos de Minas, no Alto Paranaíba. Em Lavras, no Sul do estado, os ventos chegaram a 105 km/h. Em Belo Horizonte, a velocidade máxima registrada foi de 90 km/h, no bairro Santo Agostinho.

De acordo com a empresa, os ventos costumam variar entre 40 e 45 km/h em chuvas comuns. No estado inteiro, 349 locais de votação ficaram sem luz .

A Cemig informou que cerca de três mil funcionários foram às ruas para trabalhar no restabelecimento da energia elétrica em todo o estado.

articles.title: Eleições 2026: Anderson Farias (PSD) e Sérgio Victor (Novo) votam durante a manhã no 2º turno | G1
articles.standfirst: Prefeitos das duas maiores cidades da região também falaram com a imprensa neste domingo (25).
articles.summary: Prefeitos das duas maiores cidades da região também falaram com a imprensa neste domingo (25).
articles.body:
Anderson Farias (PSD) e Sérgio Victor (Novo) votam durante a manhã no 2º turno das eleições — Foto: Foto 1: Lucas Nanini/g1 | Foto 2: Laurene Santos/TV Vanguarda

Os prefeitos das duas maiores cidades do Vale do Paraíba e região bragantina, Anderson Farias (PSD), de São José dos Campos , e Sérgio Victor (Novo), de Taubaté , aproveitaram o período da manhã para irem às urnas neste domingo (25), durante o segundo turno das eleições.

Entre os dois, Sérgio Victor foi quem votou primeiro. Ele chegou à Escola Municipal Diácono José Ângelo Victal, na região central da cidade, por volta das 9h27.

Ele conversou com a imprensa e disse que é uma oportunidade de o eleitor fazer uma escolha consciente.

"Novamente, toda eleição é uma oportunidade de a gente colocar na urna as nossas expectativas, tanto das ideias com as quais a gente concorda quanto das ideias das quais a gente discorda, e fazer uma escolha consciente. Afinal de contas, o seu voto ajuda a definir os próximos quatro anos, seja do presidente, do Congresso, nesse caso só do presidente, também no caso da prefeitura”, afirmou.

Já Anderson Farias acompanhou o vice-governador de São Paulo, Felicio Ramuth (MDB), no Colégio Sesi, antes de votar. Em seguida, ele partiu para a Escola Natural Vivência, onde conversou com a imprensa e votou por volta das 10h20.

À imprensa, Anderson diz acreditar na vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro neste domingo, por uma vantagem maior do que as pesquisas eleitorais apontam.

“A expectativa é a das mais otimistas possíveis para que realmente esse resultado se consolide, por mais que as pesquisas dão aí uma diferença muito pequena, mas eu acredito que vai ser uma diferença um pouco maior”, disse.

articles.title: Chuvas na região de Piracicaba: alagamentos e vias interditadas | G1
articles.standfirst: Cordeirópolis (SP) e Limeira (SP) registraram transtornos. Em Capivari (SP), nível do Rio também ultrapassou cota de extravasamento e vias foram interditadas.
articles.summary: Chuvas na região de Piracicaba causaram o transbordamento dos rios Capivari e Piracicaba, além de interdições em Limeira e Cordeirópolis neste domingo.
articles.body:
Chuvas afetam estradas de Cordeirópolis — Foto: Prefeitura de Cordeirópolis/Reprodução

As chuvas registradas na madrugada deste domingo (25) causaram transtornos em cidades da região de Piracicaba (SP). Em Cordeirópolis (SP), estradas municipais foram afetadas por conta do barro nas vias, especialmente no bairro do Cascalho.

De acordo com a prefeitura do município, foram registrados 88 milímetros (mm) de chuvas durante a noite de sábado (24) e a madrugada de domingo (25).

Em Limeira (SP), as pontes Preta e da Cepekelco foram interditadas preventivamente durante a madrugada e, de acordo com a Administração municipal, permanecem assim até o reestabelecimento das condições de segurança.

A Defesa Civil precisou fazer a desobstrução em uma via na região do Zé do Pote, onde caiu uma árvore e monitora as demais vias afetadas. Na cidade, foram registrados cerca de 50 mm de chuva na madrugada.

Rio Capivari — Foto: Prefeitura de Capivari

Capivari (SP) também registrou estragos.

A forte chuva, com mais de 80 milímetros de chuvas, que atingiu a cidade entre a noite de sábado (24) e a madrugada deste domingo (25), provocando no elevação do nível do Rio Capivari.

Segundo a Prefeitura de Capivari (SP), na medição realizada às 10h35 deste domingo, o rio atingiu 2,55 metros, ultrapassando a cota de extravasamento, estabelecida em 2,35 metros.

"Diante da elevação do nível do rio, o município permanece em Estado de Alerta. As equipes da Defesa Civil intensificaram o monitoramento do rio e das áreas de risco e seguem mobilizadas para adotar as medidas preventivas necessárias, conforme a evolução da situação", detalhou.

Na última quinta-feira (22), diante da previsão de fortes chuvas nas cabeceiras do Rio Capivari, a Defesa Civil solicitou à empresa Raízen a abertura total das comportas da Barragem Leopoldina. A medida preventiva teve como objetivo facilitar o escoamento da água e reduzir possíveis impactos no município.

Pontos de alagamento e interdição de vias

Em razão dos alagamentos registrados, trechos permanecem interditados para garantir a segurança da população:

Rua Miguel Assad, no bairro Nova Aparecida;

Rua Ênio Pires de Camargo, na altura do bairro São Pedro;

Rua João Vaz com Antônio Pires (Centro);

Avenida Franklina de Almeida Barros - próximo ao CFC (Rossi)

A orientação é que motoristas e pedestres respeitem as interdições e a sinalização das equipes, utilizem rotas alternativas e não tentem atravessar ruas alagadas ou locais com correnteza.

A Defesa Civil segue acompanhando a situação e continuará repassando orientações diretamente nos bairros e pelos canais oficiais da Prefeitura. A população, especialmente os moradores de áreas de risco, deve permanecer atenta às atualizações e seguir as recomendações das equipes que atuam nos locais.

Em caso de emergência, a população pode acionar a Defesa Civil pelos números 199 e (19) 3492-3186.

A Guarda Civil atende pelo telefone 153 e pelo WhatsApp (19) 3491-1311, enquanto o Corpo de Bombeiros pode ser acionado pelo 193. Os serviços de emergência funcionam 24 horas por dia, todos os dias da semana.

Em Piracicaba, o Rio que leva o nome da cidade, transbordou após atingir 4,96 metros de profundidade às 9h40 deste domingo (25), na região da Rua do Porto. Há interdições na cidade.

A Avenida Jaime Pereira está interdita nos dois sentidos. Já na Avenida Beira Rio, há bloqueios no cruzamento com a Rua Prudente de Moraes e no cruzamento com a Rua Rangel Pestana.

Não atravesse áreas alagadas nem enxurradas.

Mantenha distância de árvores, postes e fios elétricos.

Em situações de risco, procure um local seguro.

A Defesa Civil aponta que a cidade registrou 70,33 milímetros (mm) de chuva no município nas últimas 24 horas. Equipes monitoram trechos. Veja, ao final da reportagem, pontos de riscos para alagamentos na cidade.

No balanço parcial do mês, Piracicaba registrou 232,7 milímetros (mm) de chuvas entre os dias 1º e 24 de outubro.

A marca supera a média histórica de precipitação em mais que o dobro da expectativa para o período, que é de 110 milímetros, segundo dados do Posto Meteorológico Jesus Marden do Santos da Escola Superior de Agricultura “Luiz de Queiroz” (Esalq-USP).

Os pontos mencionados na reportagem são locais de recorrentes alagamentos quando ocorrem fortes pancadas de chuvas.

Avenida Jaime Pereira é tomada pela exurragada em Piracicaba neste domingo — Foto: Edijan Del Santo/EPTV

O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) emitiu alertas amarelo e laranja de perigo tempestades nas 18 cidades da área de cobertura do g1 Piracicaba e região entre este domingo e segunda-feira (26).

O aviso aponta risco de chuvas de 60 mm/hora ou 50 e 100 mm/dia, ventos intensos (60-100 km/h), e queda de granizo, bem como de corte de energia elétrica, estragos em plantações, queda de árvores e de alagamentos.

Rua Luiz de Queiroz em Piracicaba tem trechos de alagamentos — Foto: Gustavo Nolasco/ EPTV

não se abrigue debaixo de árvores, pois há risco de queda e descargas elétricas e não estacione veículos próximos a torres de transmissão e placas de propaganda

Se possível, desligue aparelhos elétricos e quadro geral de energia.

Some of the largest demonstrations have been seen in France.

Protesters there are calling for more government investment in public services.

articles.title: Eleitor vota montado em boi e chama atenção em Passos, MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Marinheiro que trabalha com passeios turísticos no Lago de Furnas foi votar acompanhado do filho e de dois bois que cria como animais de estimação em Passos (MG).
articles.summary: Eleitor vota montado em boi em Passos e leva o filho para cumprir o dever cívico acompanhado de seus animais de estimação no Sul de Minas.
articles.body:
Um eleitor de Passos (MG) chamou a atenção ao chegar para votar montado em um boi, acompanhado do filho. O marinheiro Flávio Henrique de Oliveira Lara, que trabalha com passeios de turismo no Lago de Furnas, foi até uma seção eleitoral próxima à rotatória da Avenida Juca Stockler, na entrada da cidade.

Segundo o eleitor, a iniciativa teve como objetivo unir o compromisso de votar a uma atividade que costuma realizar com o filho.

“Vim votar, vim fazer meu papel, mas vim diferente dos outros. Muito importante, porque nós decidimos o rumo que o Brasil vai pegar. A gente colocando a pessoa certa lá no poder, respinga em nós de todo jeito, na nossa população, no nosso país, tem que buscar uma melhora, aproveitar o dia de hoje. Depois que passar não tem jeito, tem que fazer o nosso papel de buscar o voto”, disse.

Flávio contou que os animais fazem parte de sua rotina e que andar com eles é uma forma de estar mais próximo do filho.

Eleitor chega a seção eleitoral montado em boi e chama atenção no Sul de Minas — Foto: Helder Almeida

“É um meio de ficar próximo do filho, eu gosto de criar. Tenho os bois como pets, mas é um pet diferente. Comprei um novinho, comecei a amansar, ele deixou montar e aconteceu isso. Depois comprei outro para andar junto do filho, o ‘trem’ foi acontecendo do nada. O pintado, é um nelore pintado, chama ‘Bordado’ e o outro chama ‘Diamante’”, afirmou.

De acordo com o eleitor, o boi chamado Bordado tem 2 anos. Já Diamante tem cerca de 1 ano e meio. Flávio também relatou que a votação foi rápida e que deixou os animais descansando enquanto esteve na seção eleitoral.

“Tava eu e meu menino. Desci, fui lá rapidinho, não tinha fila nem nada, 3 minutinhos, votei e voltei pra cá. Deitei eles na grama lá pro meu moleque ficar mais tranquilo com eles, fui lá, votei e deu tudo certo”, contou.

articles.title: Urnas desligadas no interior de SP contrariam decisão do STF | G1
articles.standfirst: Voluntários relatam falta de orientação em Taubaté e São José dos Campos após ministro Cristiano Zanin determinar a prorrogação da votação até as 19h em todo o país
articles.summary: Urnas desligadas no interior de SP em Taubaté e São José dos Campos geram confusão após o ministro Cristiano Zanin prorrogar a votação até as 19h em todo o país.
articles.body:
Em São José dos Campos, pessoas que participaram da eleição na Emef. Áurea Cantinho Rodrigues, seção 196, disseram não saber quais procedimentos deveriam ser adotados caso fosse necessário reativar os equipamentos.

No Centro de Eventos da Universidade de Taubaté (Unitau), utilizado como local de votação, a informação repassada foi de que todas as urnas já estavam na van para serem encaminhadas ao cartório eleitoral.

A orientação recebida, porém, era de que as urnas e as mídias não deixassem os pontos de votação naquele momento e que as equipes aguardassem um novo aviso.

A decisão de Zanin foi tomada neste domingo e determinou a prorrogação do encerramento da votação por duas horas em todas as seções eleitorais do país, passando das 17h para as 19h.

Campanha de Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) pediram mais cedo a prorrogação da votação em estados que haviam sido afetados por falhas, redução de frotas e cobrança indevida no transporte público e pelas chuvas.

articles.title: Vc viu? Queda de avião, atos políticos e acidente na BR-222 no MA | G1
articles.standfirst: Veja quais foram as notícias em destaque ao longo da semana no portal g1 Maranhão.
articles.summary: Veja quais foram as notícias em destaque ao longo da semana no portal g1 Maranhão.
articles.body:
Vc viu ? Queda de avião, atos políticos e acidente na BR-222 e outras notícias da semana no g1 MA — Foto: Foto: Arte/g1

Confira o resumo de algumas das principais notícias divulgadas pelo g1 Maranhão entre os dias 18 e 24 de outubro.

Uma mulher de 22 anos foi morta com um golpe de faca no pescoço no domingo (18), no bairro Vila da Paz, em Bacabal, no interior do Maranhão . O principal suspeito do crime é o companheiro dela, identificado como Mauricio Sousa, que foi encontrado ferido e levado ao hospital.

A vítima foi identificada como Francisca Clara Soares Santana. Segundo informações iniciais, vizinhos ouviram gritos de socorro e arrombaram o portão da residência. Ao entrarem no imóvel, encontraram Francisca morta e o companheiro com um ferimento no pescoço.

O Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) foi acionado e socorreu o homem, que foi levado ao Hospital Geral Laura Vasconcelos. Ele permanece internado sob custódia policial.

Um avião de pequeno porte caiu cerca de um minuto após decolar de Carutapera, no interior do Maranhão, na segunda-feira (19) . O acidente aconteceu nas proximidades do Rio do Engenho, dentro da área urbana do município. Cinco pessoas estavam a bordo da aeronave, entre elas, uma criança. Todas tiveram apenas ferimentos leves.

A aeronave, de prefixo PPS-BIT e modelo RV-10 SLA Jet, tem capacidade para quatro pessoas, mas transportava cinco no momento do acidente. A bordo estavam o empresário dono do avião, a esposa e o filho do casal, além do piloto e do copiloto.

O candidato à reeleição à Presidência da República pelo PT, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, chegou a São Luís na terça-feira (20), para cumprir agenda de campanha. Ele participou de uma mobilização com apoiadores no Centro Histórico da capital maranhense. A concentração foi marcada para as 9h, no Largo do Carmo, com início por volta das 11h.

Durante entrevista concedida na capital maranhense, Lula afirmou que seus advogados estavam apresentando à Justiça um pedido de abertura de seus sigilos bancário e telefônico e desafiou o adversário no segundo turno, o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a fazer o mesmo.

A visita de Lula ocorre cinco dias antes do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, marcado para domingo (25). O presidente esteve acompanhado de lideranças políticas nacionais e estaduais, entre elas a deputada federal reeleita por São Paulo Sônia Guajajara (PSOL), o ex-prefeito do Recife João Campos (PSB), o presidente nacional do PT, Edinho Silva, e o governador do Maranhão, Carlos Brandão (PSB).

Ainda na terça-feira, o g1 divulgou que o transporte aquaviário será gratuito durante o segundo turno das eleições de 2026, marcado para este domingo (25) , no Maranhão. A gratuidade será oferecida pelo Governo do Maranhão, por meio da Secretaria de Estado de Governo (Segov) e da Empresa Maranhense de Administração Portuária (Emap), como parte da segunda etapa da “Operação Eleições 2026”.

Ferry-boats terão viagens gratuitas no segundo turno das eleições no Maranhão; veja horários e regras — Foto: Divulgação/GOVMA

A operação será realizada entre sábado (24) e segunda-feira (26), nos terminais da Ponta da Espera e do Cujupe, além do Cais da Praia Grande e do Porto do Jacaré. O objetivo é organizar o fluxo de passageiros, reforçar a segurança e reduzir o tempo de espera para embarque.

O Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) declarou inconstitucional a cobrança de alíquotas mais altas do Imposto sobre Circulação de Mercadorias e Serviços (ICMS) sobre energia elétrica e serviços de comunicação no Maranhão. A decisão foi tomada em julgamento virtual encerrado na segunda-feira (19).

Com o entendimento, o estado não poderá aplicar sobre esses serviços uma alíquota superior à cobrada nas demais operações. A decisão tem efeitos a partir de 2024, preservando, em regra, as cobranças feitas anteriormente.

A discussão começou após a Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR) questionar uma lei estadual que previa a cobrança de 27% de ICMS sobre serviços de comunicação e sobre o consumo residencial de energia elétrica superior a 500 quilowatts-hora (kWh) por mês.

Ainda na quarta-feira, o g1 publicou que um ato em apoio à candidatura de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) à Presidência da República reuniu apoiadores na noite desta quarta-feira (21) , no Centro de São Luís . A mobilização, chamada de "Bloquinho do 22", contou com a participação do deputado federal Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG). O evento foi organizado pelos deputados federais eleitos Mariana Carvalho (PL-MA) e Aldir Júnior (PL-MA) e também contou com a presença do senador eleito Lahesio Bonfim (Novo-MA), além de outras lideranças políticas locais.

A concentração aconteceu na Praça Maria Aragão, com início às 18h. De lá, os participantes seguiram em caminhada pela Avenida Beira-Mar, no Centro da capital maranhense.

Uma mulher de 63 anos morreu após ser atropelada por um caminhão desgovernado na quarta-feira (21), no bairro da Liberdade, em São Luís . A vítima, identificada como Joelena Maria de Souza, estava sentada na porta de casa quando foi atingida pelo veículo.

Segundo a Polícia Civil do Maranhão (PC-MA), o motorista fazia uma manobra em uma rua com forte declive quando teria perdido o controle do caminhão e atingido a vítima, por volta das 16h.

Antes de atingir Joelena, o caminhão-baú desceu uma ladeira e derrubou a mureta de outra residência. Segundo familiares, a vítima ainda conseguiu empurrar o bisneto de 2 anos para dentro de casa, na tentativa de protegê-lo. A criança também foi atingida, mas está fora de perigo.

Ainda na quinta-feira, o g1 divulgou que o Tribunal Regional Eleitoral do Maranhão (TRE-MA) reduziu de 13 para seis o número de locais de votação que funcionarão em endereços diferentes no segundo turno das Eleições 2026 . A atualização foi divulgada pelo órgão após uma força-tarefa para minimizar os impactos das mudanças no estado.

A Justiça Eleitoral explicou que as mudanças têm como objetivo garantir condições adequadas de funcionamento das seções eleitorais e assegurar o direito ao voto — Foto: Tribunal Superior Eleitoral/TSE

As alterações ocorrerão nos municípios de Graça Aranha, Lima Campos, Rosário, Morros, São Mateus do Maranhão e Tutóia.

De acordo com o TRE-MA, a capital São Luís não teve nenhuma alteração nos locais de votação. Nos demais municípios do estado, os endereços também permanecem os mesmos utilizados no primeiro turno, com exceção dos seis locais informados.

Um incêndio de grandes proporções atingiu uma área de vegetação na Avenida São Luís Rei de França, no bairro Turu, em São Luís, nessa sexta-feira (23) . Equipes do Corpo de Bombeiros trabalharam no combate ao fogo desde as 16h e conseguiram controlar as chamas no início da noite.

O fogo se espalhou por uma extensa área de vegetação e chegou perto de uma garagem onde ficam veículos da Polícia Militar. Apesar do controle das chamas, uma grande quantidade de fumaça ainda era registrada na região e se espalhava pela avenida.

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, o tempo seco favoreceu a propagação do incêndio. A causa do fogo ainda não foi identificada.

Segundo informações da Polícia Rodoviária Federal (PRF), o acidente aconteceu em um trecho da rodovia entre os municípios de Itapecuru-Mirim e Vargem Grande e envolveu uma van de transporte de passageiros e um carro de passeio, que colidiram frontalmente.

Com o impacto da colisão, a van saiu da pista, enquanto o outro veículo ficou no acostamento. De acordo com a PRF, duas pessoas ficaram presas às ferragens.

articles.title: Idoso com infecção urinária decide votar antes de ir ao hospital | G1
articles.standfirst: Mesmo com quadro de infecção urinária, aposentado fez questão de votar na E. E. Professor Euzebio Antonio Rodrigues, em Hortolândia. Idoso disse quer "vida mais confortável".
articles.summary: Mesmo com quadro de infecção urinária, aposentado fez questão de votar na E. E. Professor Euzebio Antonio Rodrigues, em Hortolândia. Idoso disse quer "vida mais confortável".
articles.body:
Os 90 anos já poderiam ser um desafio para Francisco Molina sair de casa para votar no 2º turno das eleições gerais de 2026, realizado neste domingo (25). Mas mesmo com um quadro de infecção urinária , o aposentado fez questão de enfrentar as escadas da Escola Estadual Professor Euzebio Antonio Rodrigues, em Hortolândia (SP), para participar do pleito.

"Com certeza, eu não deveria votar agora. Nem poderia, por causa da minha situação física. Mas eu estou vindo aqui para votar para mudança", comentou.

➡️ No Brasil, o voto é obrigatório para pessoas alfabetizadas maiores de 18 e menores de 70 anos — portanto o aposentado não teria qualquer problema de não participar.

Francisco Molina encarou a escada da E. E. Prof. Euzebio Antônio Rodrigues, em Hortolândia, para votar — Foto: Charlise Alves/g1

A determinação fez Francisco relembrar de 1961, quando participou da campanha de Jânio Quadros à presidência da República . "Eu subia num caminhão com uma vassorinha na frente. Eu vivi em um Brasil diferente", relatou.

O idoso contou que, após a votação, iria ao hospital para passar em consulta e continuar o tratamento. Segundo ele, a motivação é resgatar o Brasil que eu viveu quando solteiro e conquistar "uma vida de mais saúde e mais voltada a Deus e a Jesus Cristo".

"Quero um Brasil da pátria, da família e, principalmente, um Brasil que ofereça aos nossos filhos, aos nossos netos, até eu que já tenho bisnetos, uma vida mais confortável", disse.

Mais de 2,5 milhões de eleitores voltam às urnas neste domingo (25) nas 31 cidades da área de cobertura do g1 Campinas. A votação ocorre das 8h às 17h, e os eleitores irão escolher o presidente da República pelos próximos quatro anos.

articles.title: Eleições em Campinas: famílias com votos opostos pregam respeito | G1
articles.standfirst: Com camisas do Brasil e roupas vermelhas, apoiadores de Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula chegaram ao mesmo tempo ao local de votação neste domingo (25).
articles.summary: Eleições em Campinas: apoiadores de candidatos opostos se encontraram na escola com a disputa mais acirrada da cidade e deram exemplo de civilidade.
articles.body:
Camisa do Brasil de um lado, roupa vermelha do outro. Duas famílias que não se conheciam, mas tinham preferências políticas bem diferentes, chegaram ao mesmo tempo à Escola Estadual Dr. Telêmaco Paioli Melges, em Campinas (SP), neste domingo (25), para votar no segundo turno das eleições.

A coincidência aconteceu justamente na escola que teve a disputa mais acirrada de Campinas no primeiro turno. De um lado, Amara Alves e o genro Guilherme Henrique, apoiadores de Flávio Bolsonaro. Do outro, Andréia e Marco Silva, que torcem pela vitória de Lula.

As duas famílias também tinham algo em comum: levaram as crianças para acompanhar a votação. E, apesar da rivalidade nas urnas, o encontro foi marcado pelo respeito.

Famílias com votos opostos se encontram na escola com disputa mais acirrada de Campinas (SP) — Foto: Igor Henrique Silva

Amara já tinha votado em Sumaré (SP), onde mora, mas foi até Campinas para acompanhar o genro Guilherme, que vota na escola. Os netos também participaram do passeio eleitoral.

"Eu já votei, que eu voto lá no Matão, sou de Sumaré. Ele vota aqui em Campinas, vim trazer ele para exercer a função dele. Não dá para a gente cobrar se a gente não votar", contou.

Ao perceber que a família ao lado tinha uma preferência política diferente, Amara deixou claro que isso não era motivo para discussão. "Eu sou desse lado, eles são desse e o respeito é mútuo" , afirmou.

Ela também fez questão de registrar sua posição. "Essa bandeira que eu estou vestindo aqui não é nem de partido, nem de nada, é do Brasil. O importante é brigar pelo Brasil, não por partido", disse.

De vermelho, Andréia e Marco Silva também chegaram acompanhados da família. Os filhos e uma sobrinha foram junto para a votação.

"A gente tá do lado do Brasil, né? A gente não tem lado político. A gente tá do lado do Brasil pela democracia", declarou Marco.

Questionado sobre a presença das crianças, ele explicou que quer incentivar a participação política desde cedo.

"É importante para ele ver desde cedo o lado certo, né? Pra não crescer e ir pro outro lado errado", brincou.

articles.title: Vice-prefeita de Jaboatão, Irmã Babate morre aos 73 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Professora e ex-vereadora estava na gestão municipal pelo Partido Liberal (PL), ao lado do prefeito Mano Medeiros (PSD).
articles.summary: Professora e ex-vereadora estava na gestão municipal pelo Partido Liberal (PL), ao lado do prefeito Mano Medeiros (PSD).
articles.body:
Irmã Babate, vice-prefeita de Jaboatão dos Guararapes, morreu aos 73 anos — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Morreu na manhã deste domingo (25) Irmã Babate ( PL ), vice-prefeita de Jaboatão dos Guararapes , no Grande Recife . Josabete Maria da Silva tinha 73 anos e atuou por mais de três décadas como professora antes de entrar na política.

Ela também já foi vereadora de Jaboatão, antes de se candidatar a vice-prefeita na chapa do atual prefeito, Mano Medeiros ( PSD ). A causa da morte não foi informada, mas ela estava hospitalizada desde o dia 10 de outubro.

Em nota de pesar, a prefeitura lembrou que Irmã Babate era uma "mulher de fé inabalável" que "dedicou sua vida a servir a igreja, ao cuidado com as pessoas e às causas sociais".

Irmã Babate é filha do Pastor José Leoncio. Com seu marido, José Amaro, teve cinco filhos. A vice-prefeita deixa também seis netos e duas bisnetas.

No dia 10 de outubro, a família de Irmã Babate publicou um comunicado nas redes sociais dizendo que ela estava hospitalizada. Na ocasião, foi informado que a vice-prefeita faria um procedimento médico.

O prefeito de Jaboatão dos Guararapes publicou nota de pesar em suas redes sociais neste domingo (25). "Tive a honra de caminhar ao seu lado e compartilhar momentos importantes da história da nossa cidade", diz o comunicado de Mano Medeiros.

A governadora de Pernambuco, Raquel Lyra (PSD) também lamentou a morte da vice-prefeita. Em nota, afirmou que "Irmã Babate deixa um legado em defesa da educação, das causas sociais e do compromisso com sua gente".

O velório da ex-prefeita foi marcado para as 16h deste domingo (25), na igreja Assembleia de Deus de Cavaleiro. Já o sepultamento está previsto para às 12h da segunda-feira (26), no cemitério Parque das Flores, no Sancho, na Zona Oeste do Recife.

articles.title: US Marine indicted for robbing and murdering Japanese woman in Okinawa
articles.summary: Conviction on murder and robbery charges carries the death penalty or life imprisonment in Okinawa
articles.body:
A US marine has been indicted in Okinawa prefecture in Japan on charges of robbing and murdering a Japanese woman.

Lance corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, was accused of killing Anna Yagi, 39 , in a hotel in the prefecture 's capital Naha and taking her wallet and backpack earlier this month. Ballard denied the allegations.

Ballard, who was stationed at Futenma Air Base, was found walking alone in Okinawa city later that day and was arrested the following day on suspicion of robbery and murder.

He was indicted on Sunday amid growing anger among Okinawa residents over the incident and the presence of US military installations.

He allegedly strangled the woman with the cord of a telephone in a hotel room between 2.10 and 4.15am on 3 October and stole her backpack that contained her wallet and other belongings, according to the indictment.

The woman had checked into the hotel with a man around 2.10am that day. Hotel employees entered the room at 4.15am after she did not check out on time. The staff found her body and alerted the police, investigative sources told the Japan Times .

Investigators later checked the security footage that showed a man with tattoos on both arms and a backpack leading the hotel, the report said. The backpack was found near the hotel.

Under Japanese law, conviction can carry the death penalty or life imprisonment.

The incident involving a foreign national prompted Okinawa governor Genta Koja to step up calls for the central government to take preventive measures.

Local residents have long voiced anger over crimes committed by US military personnel, including offences against women and girls, as well as noise and pollution associated with American military installations.

Following his arrest, the US military in Okinawa imposed a 30-day curfew on 9 October, restricting personnel from leaving their bases between midnight and 5 am.

It was after the Japanese government lodged a strong protest with the US government over the incident.

Prime minister Sanae Takaichi condemned the incident as a "brutal and heinous" crime and called for stricter discipline of American personnel.

The incident renewed long-standing local tensions over the heavy US military presence on Okinawa, which hosts a large share of US bases in Japan.

Crimes involving US military personnel stationed in Japan, including murder, rape, and robbery, have long been a source of public concern.

In Okinawa, local police handled over 100 criminal cases involving US personnel in 2025 alone, according to an official from the prefecture.

In 2016, a former Marine and Kadena base civilian worker Kenneth Gadson was sentenced to life in prison for raping and murdering a 20-year-old woman.

The rape of a ​12-year-old Okinawan ⁠girl by three US servicemen in 1995 sparked widespread protests.

He has also highlighted Arizona's water security, criticised Trump's tariffs and pledged to oppose data-centre projects over concerns about their water consumption.His medical background could help him appeal to voters concerned about health-care affordability. articles.title: US midterms 2026: Who is Ami Bera, Indian-American Democrat seeking re-election from California's newly redrawn district
articles.summary: Indian-American Democratic Congressman Ami Bera is seeking re-election to the US House of Representatives in the November 3, 2026, general election, but
articles.body: Indian-American Democratic Congressman Ami Bera is seeking re-election to the US House of Representatives in the November 3, 2026, general election, but will contest from California's newly redrawn 3rd Congressional District instead of the 6th District he currently represents.Bera will face Republican candidate Robb Tucker, a member of the Nevada County Board of Supervisors, in the race. The 3rd District covers large parts of Placer, El Dorado and Nevada counties and extends into the city of Sacramento.Bera, who lives in Elk Grove, California, has represented the state in Congress since 2013. He is the longest-serving Indian-American member of the US Congress and serves on the House Foreign Affairs Committee and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence.Who is Ami Bera?Born in Los Angeles to Indian immigrant parents with roots in Gujarat, Bera is a physician by training and a lifelong Californian. He earned his bachelor's degree and medical degree from the University of California, Irvine.After graduating from medical school in 1991, he completed his residency in internal medicine at California Pacific Medical Center, where he eventually became chief resident. He then practised medicine in the Sacramento area and held leadership positions in healthcare management.Bera later served as medical director of care management at Mercy Healthcare, where he developed strategies to improve care across its seven-hospital system. He also served as chief medical officer for Sacramento County, focusing on healthcare access, affordability and job creation.He subsequently joined the University of California, Davis, as a clinical professor of medicine and associate dean for admissions and outreach, helping train future doctors and support community healthcare initiatives.Bera's political career and prioritiesBera was first elected to the US House in 2012 and took office in January 2013. He has since won re-election six times, building a political career centred on healthcare, economic opportunity and public service.In Congress, he serves on the House Foreign Affairs Committee as ranking member of its Subcommittee on East Asia and the Pacific. He is also a member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and the New Democrat Coalition, a group of Democrats that advocates economic growth, innovation and fiscal responsibility.Bera has said his experience as a doctor shapes his approach to public service, with an emphasis on listening to constituents and working across party lines.His congressional office says it has helped return more than $23 million to local taxpayers through assistance with issues such as delayed veterans' benefits and Social Security payments. It has also helped more than 36,000 Sacramento County residents since 2013.Bera currently represents California's 6th Congressional District, which lies entirely within Sacramento County. Following changes to California's congressional district boundaries, he decided to run in the 3rd District in the 2026 election.The contest will pit Bera against Tucker, a Republican who serves on the Nevada County Board of Supervisors. The outcome will determine who represents the district in the US House for the next term.Bera has lived in Sacramento County for more than three decades with his wife, Janine, who is also a physician. articles.title: Beyond diagnosis: Breast cancer’s hidden financial burden
articles.summary: Breast cancer care in Bengaluru leaves many families financially strained: 84% face catastrophic costs, loans and 49 visits; experts urge better insurance and support.
articles.body: Bengaluru: For a woman diagnosed with breast cancer, the battle is not just within the walls of the hospital. Be it a working woman who has to take a loss of pay during treatment or a homemaker from a village who has to make multiple trips to the hospital, dipping into her savings, oncologists in Bengaluru highlight how financial distress is forcing some women to delay treatment, miss follow-up appointments and reconsider expensive therapies.Citing an Indian study of 500 breast cancer patients at Tata Memorial Centre, published in the International Journal for Equity in Health, doctors noted that 84.2% of households experienced catastrophic health expenditure, while 72.4% resorted to distress financing. The study found that 14% of patients discontinued treatment during the study period, with financial problems accounting for 4.8% of all patients. They also cited figures indicating that out-of-pocket treatment expenditure was over Rs 1.8 lakh. Patients made an average of 49 hospital visits over 276 days, while approximately 69% had taken loans by the end of the follow-up period.Dr Monika Pansari, consultant – breast and gynaecology onco-surgery (surgical oncology) and robotic surgery, Manipal Hospital, Kanakapura Road, said the financial burden could persist for years after initial treatment. “Some patients are at risk of losing their job as a result of the cancer diagnosis. The expenses may increase just when she may be losing her income,” she said, adding that follow-up tests, medicines and rehabilitation continue to strain household budgets.The burden is particularly severe for women who are primary earners or work in the informal sector without paid medical leave. Dr Anil Kamath, senior surgical oncologist at Apollo Hospitals, Bannerghatta, said treatment could span six months to a year, during which fatigue, nausea and other side effects could affect a woman’s ability to work.“Even people who have insurance face problems because insurance coverage is not keeping pace with the rising cost of medical treatment,” he said, pointing to the growing costs of newer therapies such as immunotherapy and targeted therapy.He added, “Modern treatment can cost minimum Rs 30-40 lakh. Therefore, families need to recognise the importance of having higher insurance coverage.”Dr MS Sushruta, senior consultant – surgical oncology, breast and gynaec oncology, Cytecare Hospitals, added the financial burden includes expenses that are often overlooked, such as travel, accommodation, food, childcare and the loss of income for family members accompanying patients. “These expenses, coupled with existing family responsibilities and other personal circumstances, can make the treatment journey extremely stressful and affect a patient’s ability to adhere to the prescribed treatment plan,” she said.Doctors called for changes across healthcare delivery, insurance coverage and workplace policies to prevent financial distress among women undergoing treatment. “Financial counselling should begin at diagnosis; insurance should cover treatment and follow-up care more comprehensively, and support should extend to travel and caregiving costs. articles.title: Modi revives ‘phone banking’ charge against Cong; warns of cyberthreats to economy
articles.summary: PM Modi in Bhubaneswar revives ‘phone banking’ charge against Congress, warns of cyber threats; inaugurates RBI Tier IV data centre, cyber training institute.
articles.body: Bhubaneswar: Blaming the Congress for allowing politically connected borrowers to secure loans worth thousands of crores prior to 2014, and pushing banks to deal with non-performing assets (NPAs), Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said his govt has democratised access to financial services, while warning that cyber terrorists pose a growing threat to the economy and national security.“There was an era of phone banking when some special people in Delhi and those connected to them received loans worth thousands of crores through a phone call, while poor and middle-class families needed guarantees even to open bank accounts,” PM said after inaugurating the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in the city.Claiming that politically connected individuals benefited from easy access to bank loans before 2014, Modi said the country’s financial system had suffered because of indiscriminate lending to a select group of influential borrowers. Modi said the resulting bad loans pushed banks into a deep NPA crisis.Contrasting the previous system with the current govt’s emphasis on digital banking, PM said his govt has brought millions into the formal banking network.Modi cited initiatives such as Jan Dhan Yojana, Mudra loans, PM SVANidhi and PM Vishwakarma as examples of efforts that expanded financial inclusion and enabled first-time entrepreneurs, street vendors, artisans and self-help groups to access institutional credit. Referring to direct benefit transfer mechanisms, he said funds now reach beneficiaries directly, eliminating leakages that were once common in welfare delivery.PM also stressed the need to secure India’s digital financial infrastructure as cyber threats become increasingly sophisticated. “If a country has to be weakened, it can also be done by attacking its economy,” he said, adding that the nation’s banking system must be protected from “cyber looters and cyber terrorists”.He said modern conflicts are no longer fought solely with conventional weapons and that financial and cyber resilience have become critical elements of national security. Emerging threats require modern infrastructure, advanced computing capabilities and up-to-date training systems, making the RBI’s new facilities particularly significant.Highlighting Odisha’s growing role in India’s technology-driven growth story, Modi said the state was evolving “from mines to microchips”, with investments expanding in semiconductors, electronics, data centres and advanced computing. He added that eastern India, especially Odisha, was emerging as an important growth engine for a developed India.Speaking on the occasion, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said India aspires to build a financial system “that the world trusts and every Indian can rely upon”. She described the new Bhubaneswar campus as a significant step towards that goal.Spread across 18.55 acres and built at a cost of Rs 170 crore, the facility has been designed to meet RBI’s growing computing requirements while providing a secure, scalable and resilient digital ecosystem. The campus houses four state-of-the-art data centres that will host mission-critical payment and settlement systems and other key RBI functions.Officials said the facility is certified to the Uptime Institute’s Tier IV standard, the highest global benchmark for data-centre infrastructure and operational resilience, making it one of the largest such facilities in the global banking and financial services sector.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhubaneswar | Silver Rate in Bhubaneswar | Bank Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Public Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Petrol Price in Bhubaneswar | Diesel Price in Bhubaneswar | CNG Price in Bhubaneswar | LPG Price in BhubaneswarStay updated with the latest Bhubaneswar news. articles.summary: 202nd Kittur Utsav in Belagavi concluded after three days, marking Rani Chennamma’s victory with a 4km procession, cultural shows, seminars and livestock fair.
articles.body: Belagavi: The 202nd Kittur Utsav, commemorating the historic victory of Rani Channamma against the British, concluded on Sunday after three days of celebrations.Kittur utsav was celebrated as a symbol of the victory in which the Kittur army defeated the British on Oct 23, 1824. Utsav featured seminars on heritage and literature, cultural performances, sports events, livestock shows and exhibitions. Thousands of visitors from across the country participated. The event also showcased emerging talent alongside established artistes, drawing appreciation despite criticism over the lack of new attractions.A four kilometre-long grand procession, which was held with artists representing Dollu, Yakshagana Band, Tiger-costume, Gombe Kunita and others, reflected the pride of Kittur Karnataka. Art troupes from Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Keralam also participated in the procession. The entire procession reflected the multiculturalism of South India. ‘Om Parashakti’ troupe from Keralam was the highlight of the parade. People celebrated by clicking selfies with the mythical costumes. 501 women carried a Poorna Kumbh, Kalash at the front of the procession.Inauguration by pro farmer activist:Pro-farmer activist Chukki Nanjundaswamy, who inaugurated the Kittur festival on Friday evening, said that women gained independence from the British. But girls did not have the freedom to be born in this country. She reminded that thefemale foeticide is increasing every year.Chukki slammed the event organisers for not giving more space to women on stage.She urged that an education policy to be implemented that allows girls to receive education at least up to PUC. Expressing concern about the country’s farmers, she warned that Karnataka ranks second in farmer suicides and the govt must take responsibility for the dire situation.Programme diversity:Previously, Kittur utsav was limited to cultural, literary, and sporting activities. This year’s utsav attracted attention with exhibitions, and livestock fairs.Ravi Saligoudar, District Deputy Director of the Animal Husbandry Department, said that the exhibition of various breeds of cattle, bulls, buffaloes, rams, sheep, chickens, and pigs was a centercentre of attraction.Khilari breed, foreign HF breed and Gir breed of cows, Hallikar and Amrut Mahal breeds of bulls, Jafferbadi, Mahesana, Murra, Surti breeds of buffaloes, Darfur, Yalaga breed rams, Shirohi breed goats, Landrez, Duroc, Yorkshire breed pigs, and indigenous Turkish breed chickens were on display. The exhibition, which featured over 500 animals, was an attraction.Cultural splendour:A variety of cultural programmes attracted the spectators. Chandan Shetty and Shamita Malnad and team presented a musical programme on the first day, followed by Rajesh Krishnan and team on the second day and Arjun Janya and team on the third day.Stay updated with the latest Hubballi news. articles.title: Baylor fires Dave Aranda after third loss of season, will reportedly owe him substantial buyout
articles.summary: Dave Aranda's firing triggers a roughly $12 million buyout after a contract extension through 2029, making him the third Power Four coach axed this year.
articles.body: The Baylor Bears have moved on from head coach Dave Aranda after losing to Kansas 25-24 on the road Saturday in what was their second straight loss and third defeat of the season. Aranda was in the midst of his seventh season in charge of the Bears after taking over the head coaching gig in Waco, Texas, ahead of the 2020 season. After going 2-7 in his first season, one plagued by COVID, he led Baylor to a 12-2 campaign in 2021 that included a Sugar Bowl victory over a 10-win Ole Miss team. Baylor finished as the No. 5 team in the country in the final AP Top 25 Poll that season. Baylor officially announced the news of Aranda's departure on Sunday afternoon. "He is a gifted coach and a brilliant football mind whose leadership brought some of our best Baylor football memories. While this is a difficult moment, we believe a change in leadership is necessary at this time for our program. We will forever be thankful to Dave and his family for their time here at Baylor, and we wish them well." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE While it's safe to say Aranda would have liked to have kept his job, in today's college football, the majority of coaches who are fired are subject to a hefty buyout, and that appears to be the case for the 50-year-old. Aranda inked a contract extension in 2022 that ran through the end of the 2029 season. Now, his firing triggers a buyout package of around $12 million, according to Yahoo's Ross Dellenger. Baylor's three losses this season have come by a combined 13 points. Baylor defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman will be taking over as interim coach at Baylor. Aranda is now the third Power Four coach to be fired during the current college football season. Maryland fired head coach Mike Locksley earlier in the week, while NC State parted ways with Dave Doeren following the Wolfpack's loss to Stanford on October 23. articles.title: Reckless visitors are destroying Yellowstone's iconic thermal pools with trash
articles.summary: That's a lot of garbage: Yellowstone National Park's geology team collected over 23,000 pieces of trash from geysers and hot springs, including AirPods and rubber ducks.
articles.body: A team at Yellowstone National Park has collected over 23,000 pieces of trash as of early October, plus an array of unique items like international coins, golf tees and an inhaler, from geysers, hot springs, boardwalks and surrounding areas. Aside from paper and plastic debris, the Yellowstone Geology Program retrieved roughly 10,700 rocks and sticks, more than 360 hats and plenty of camera lens caps, hair ties and pacifiers, National Geographic reported. Other quirky finds included five AirPods, three Delta flight pins and a singular Uno card, as well as dental retainers and rubber ducks. MASSIVE BISON RAMS PICKUP TRUCK IN YELLOWSTONE AFTER DRIVER TRIES TO AVOID COLLISION It has been a record-setting year for trash collection, which is managed by the park’s geology team. The team is trained in safe hydrothermal navigation practices, according to the Yellowstone Volcano Observatory. In 2025, Yellowstone welcomed over 4.7 million visitors, according to the National Park Service. With such a large volume of people coming into the park, debris builds up, especially in high-traffic areas like Old Faithful and the Midway Geyser Basin. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Some of the garbage that’s collected, such as food wrappers and maps, is possibly deposited unintentionally, swept away by the park’s strong winds. "We believe that most of those are accidental," Margery Price, a physical science technician with the Yellowstone National Park Geology Program, told National Geographic. Any type of foreign material can harm a hydrothermal feature, either by clogging the water supply, polluting the water or blocking its runoff channel, according to the Yellowstone Volcano Observatory. Even natural materials like rocks and sticks still need to be removed, as they can cause clogging. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Trash can also change the chemistry of the springs. Chemicals from microplastics can enter the water and affect the microbes that live in the pools and provide them with their distinctive hues. Morning Glory Pool, named after the blue flower, changed color in the 20th century due to trash and various foreign items being tossed in by park visitors. Staff even called the pool the "garbage can" beginning in the 1950s, according to the observatory. The debris tossed into the pool cooled the water temperature and allowed orange and yellow-colored bacteria to grow, altering the spring's clear blue appearance. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ In hopes of restoring the water's blue hue, park rangers partially drained Morning Glory in the 1970s to extract debris. The pool's original color, alas, did not fully return. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital reached out to Yellowstone National Park for comment.

articles.title: Cornell fraternity member seeks dismissal from Jane Doe’s sexual assault lawsuit
articles.summary: One of the men sued by a former Cornell University student identified as Jane Doe has asked a judge to dismiss the claims against him, arguing that her allegations do not support her broader accusations of rape and sexual assault.
articles.body: One of the men sued by a former Cornell University student identified as Jane Doe has asked a judge to dismiss the claims against him, arguing that her allegations do not support her broader accusations of rape and sexual assault. Diego Sarabia filed the motion Friday seeking dismissal of all claims against him in the lawsuit Doe filed Sept. 16 in New York state court. Sarabia, who was a member of the Chi Phi fraternity, was one of seven men originally sued by Doe for allegedly participating in a gang rape at the Chi Phi house from Oct. 19 to 20, 2024. Sarabia denies the allegations against him, according to the filing. His attorneys argue that even if the complaint’s factual allegations are accepted as true for the purposes of the motion, the claims against him were filed too late, are legally insufficient, or both. James C. Knox, an attorney for Sarabia, wrote in the motion that as far as the allegations against his client, “this is essentially a lawsuit about a forced kiss.” Knox argued that the conduct Doe attributed to Sarabia did not qualify for the extended statue of limitations she cited for certain sexual offenses. Doe accused Sarabia of grabbing her face, kissing her and snorting ketamine off her body with other fraternity members during a drug and alcohol-fueled encounter in what was known as the “alumni room” of the fraternity house. “Throughout a sprawling complaint approaching 600 paragraphs, plaintiff repeatedly, collectively and without differentiation accuses seven student defendants of ‘sexual assault and rape,’” Knox wrote in his filing. “Those legally conclusory statements do not substitute for pleaded facts.” Knox argued that the complaint did not allege that Sarabia “supplied her with drugs or alcohol, participated in any of the alleged sexual encounters described elsewhere in the complaint, or was even present for most of the conduct that forms the basis of plaintiff’s broader allegations.” The attorney said that the assault, battery and intentional infliction of emotional distress claims were barred by a one-year statute of limitations and the allegations against Sarabia did not qualified for extensions cited in the complaint. Doe’s attorney Thomas Giuffra declined to comment on Sunday. Giuffra previously agreed to withdraw claims against the acting president of the fraternity’s chapter at the time. The lawsuit inspired calls for a reckoning at the Ivy League institution, where past and current students and community members have accused the administration of not doing enough to protect women from sexual assault. Cornell’s Board of Trustees hired former Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates “to lead a comprehensive independent review of how the University prevents and responds to sexual harassment, sexual assault and related misconduct on campus.” Doe’s allegations were investigated by Cornell University Police. An internal civil rights investigation led to the expulsion of two students and disciplinary action against others. Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten declined to bring charges in November 2024 based on a six-page statement in which Doe described some of the sexual conduct that night as consensual. Van Houten declined to evaluate other investigative materials that had been gathered by investigators, including other witness statements. Gov. Kathy Hochul called the evaluation inadequate and recently appointed state Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor to investigate the allegations. James’ office has started that process. The attorney general is expected to hire outside investigators to assist with the effort. Two of the accused men are seeking to disqualify James from overseeing the investigation based on a comment she made on social media about the case before she was tapped to run the probe. They argued the state’s top law enforcement official had prejudged the case. Both challenges are still pending. James has deflected calls to step down from the case and has said she is “committed to leading a comprehensive investigation they can trust, guided only by the facts, the evidence, and the law.”

articles.title: Venezuela’s opposition leader Machado returns after months in exile, as doubts over democracy deepen
articles.summary: Opposition leader and Nobel laureate María Corina Machado reappeared in Venezuela Sunday for the first time since December, returning from exile at a time when doubts about the country’s democratic future — and the role of the U.S. — are growing.
articles.body: CARACAS, Venezuela — Opposition leader and Nobel laureate María Corina Machado reappeared in Venezuela Sunday for the first time since December, returning from exile at a time when doubts about the country’s democratic future — and the role of the U.S. — are growing. It was her first appearance since the U.S. military deposed the country’s then-President Nicolás Maduro, replacing him with an interim president who has exceeded the time she was authorized to serve, with no election scheduled. Machado announced her arrival on social media, writing, “I am here. With you.” Another leading figure in the Venezuelan opposition, Edmundo González, wrote on X confirming that Machado had arrived and that he would be next to her “very soon.” “Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!” he wrote. “You know it, this is until the end.” Venezuela run by Maduro ally backed by the Trump administration On Sunday afternoon, Machado strode into a church in the town of Lara, west of Caracas, to the applause of dozens gathered there as they shook her hand and hugged her, with cell phones aloft to record her return. “María! María!” someone cried out. “Welcome to Venezuela!” another person shouted. Asked by reporters Sunday about Machado’s return to Venezuela, U.S. President Donald Trump said, “I don’t know anything about it, but I think she’s a very nice woman. She gave me her Nobel Prize. So how can I say anything else? And I hope she’s safe. She’s a very nice woman. But we’re doing really well in Venezuela.” Since Maduro’s ouster, Venezuela has been run by acting President Delcy Rodríguez, a longtime Maduro ally who received the Trump administration’s blessing to succeed him. Rodríguez was initially supposed to serve only 90 days as acting president, but has remained in office and has made no move to call an election. Machado was briefly detained in January 2025, following a protest against Maduro’s planned swearing-in ceremony, and went into hiding in Venezuela for 11 months. After making a clandestine escape from the country, she reappeared that December in Norway, where she was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for her peaceful challenge to Maduro’s authoritarian government. Machado and her allies have been demanding a date for a presidential election in Venezuela, but U.S. officials have emphasized economic stabilization first. Credible evidence shows the opposition won the last election In October 2023, Machado won an opposition primary and intended to challenge Maduro in the 2024 presidential election, but the government barred her from running for office. González took her place on the ballot, and ample credible evidence showed that he defeated Maduro by more than a 2-to-1 margin. But the National Electoral Council, which is stacked with ruling-party loyalists, declared Maduro the winner. The lead-up and aftermath of the election were marked by widespread government repression, including forced disappearances, torture and other human rights violations. More than 2,000 people, including poll workers, were detained in the days after the vote. In January, the U.S. military captured Maduro in Caracas and whisked him to New York to face drug-related charges, which he has denied. Many Venezuelans were stunned by the Trump administration’s decision to work with Rodríguez, instead of Machado, to try to revitalize the crisis-racked country. Machado has demanded a date for a presidential election Machado had repeatedly vowed to return to Venezuela and, according to her party, she made seven unsuccessful attempts. One of the efforts would have seen her take a charter boat, but the operator canceled the trip, alleging the vessel was unfit for navigation. In another attempt, her team said, Machado tried to fly to the Caribbean island of Curacao, from where she could take a speedboat to Venezuela, but her plane was denied landing permits. Opposition activists have accused Venezuela’s government of blocking Machado’s return, a claim denied by Venezuelan authorities. Others have also questioned whether the Trump administration has also been involved in the efforts to stop her from returning. Trump administration officials deny they are holding Machado back but have said that, on some occasions, they have advised her against returning due to safety concerns. After Maduro was deposed, Venezuela’s highest court said Rodríguez could serve as acting president for up to 90 days — an interim appointment that could be extended by the National Assembly for an additional 90 days. But the ruling party-controlled assembly never voted to extend her term. Machado and her allies have demanded that the Rodríguez government set a date for a presidential election. Rodríguez told the U.N. General Assembly in September that Venezuelans will determine the “right moment” for the next election. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has argued that before holding new elections, Venezuela must stabilize its economy and rebuild its institutions, including its courts and electoral council. But he said in a news conference earlier this month that Machado has “every right to enter her country whenever she wants to return.” Supporters of Machado have held demonstrations in Caracas demanding her return.

articles.title: AI’s ‘opportunity divide’ could deepen global inequality, UN official warns
articles.summary: The deputy secretary-general of UN’s ICT agency says unequal access to AI means poorer nations may be left behind.
articles.body:
Doha, Qatar – Artificial intelligence (AI) risks widening the gap between rich and poor countries, potentially deepening existing social and economic inequalities, a senior United Nations official has warned.

Developing countries face significant barriers to benefitting from the AI revolution, Tomas Lamanauskas, the deputy secretary-general of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), a UN agency focused on information and communication technologies, told Al Jazeera.

“There is a risk … I think the AI divide is really the big concern because it’s really not just about the digital divide,” Lamanauskas said on the sidelines of the UN Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) World Investment Forum in Doha, Qatar on Sunday.

“AI has the huge potential of powering health, education, public services, industries, agriculture, trade. So a great divide could really mean an opportunity divide, and really could deepen the socioeconomic divide,” he said.

Lamanauskas said the disparities are already evident in digital infrastructure, citing the examples of Africa and Latin America, which together account for just 3.3 percent of global data centre capacity.

“So you clearly see still a rather big infrastructure divide,” he said, adding that 2.2 billion people worldwide remain without internet access.

In a December 2025 report , the UN Development Programme (UNDP) cautioned that AI could trigger a new era of inequality between nations, reversing decades of progress in narrowing economic disparities between nations.

The UNDP warned that countries with unreliable power, limited connectivity, and a lack of technological skills risk missing out on the economic gains of AI.

Bridging the digital infrastructure gap would require an estimated $2.8 trillion in investment by 2030, UN official Lamanauskas said.

The divide between nations is also evident in the adoption of AI, he added. While approximately 29 percent of working-age people in developed countries use generative AI, that figure drops to 16 percent in developing nations.

“This actually affects your ability to be productive and to be part of job-market opportunities,” Lamanauskas said.

Lamanauskas acknowledged growing concerns about AI-driven job losses, citing estimates that the technology could displace 90 million jobs, but also create 170 million new ones.

However, he warned that even if there is a “net positive impact”, many people will personally experience disruption, as an estimated 40 percent of workplace skills could change by 2030.

He also pointed to language inequalities, revealing that only seven percent of African languages are represented in AI translation tools, limiting access for millions of potential users.

According to the 2026 International AI Safety Report released in February, about one billion people use AI for a variety of tasks, including seeking guidance on medical health and writing.

While no concrete data exists, the report estimated that about 60 percent of jobs in advanced economies and 40 percent in emerging economies could be exposed to AI-related impacts.

“The fears are real,” said Fazl Barez, a senior researcher at the University of Oxford specialising in AI safety and governance.

However, he cautioned that it was important to distinguish between AI “automating tasks and replacing entire jobs”.

“What are the types of jobs that could be lost? Those involving routine cognitive work are particularly exposed, but the scale remains uncertain,” Barez told Al Jazeera.

“AI-driven automation threatens to erode government tax bases, lower living standards, and disempower citizens.”

Despite concerns around the AI revolution, Lamanauskas said he did not believe there was a “possibility just to stop AI” or halt its rapid advancement.

“AI is here to stay, and AI is here to transform our lives,” he said, noting that 104 countries now have AI strategies, compared with just four a decade ago.

“AI is not a technology that can be controlled by one person or organisation or one company,” the UN official added.

Nevertheless, he called for greater investment in digital infrastructure, education and regulation to ensure developing countries can participate in helping shape the technology.

“The way forward is really to invest to make sure that the AI benefits everyone, to recognise and acknowledge the fears and anxieties that people feel,” he said.

articles.title: Trump reveals dire warning to Macron as violent unrest spreads across Europe
articles.summary: Trump says he warned Emmanuel Macron that immigration policies were "destroying France" as nearly 1,000 protesters were arrested on Saturday.
articles.body: President Donald Trump said he warned French President Emmanuel Macron that his immigration policies were "destroying France" as he raised concerns about unrest across Europe during an interview on "Sunday Morning Futures." "I told Macron, when I first came in, I met him early. I said, 'You are destroying France. You're letting people come in that hate your country,'" Trump told Larry Kudlow. Trump criticized France for allowing people into the country who he said opposed French culture and national identity. He also pointed to unrest in Spain and Italy while arguing that his administration's border enforcement policies had prevented similar problems in the United States. "The people that are causing the problems are people that hate Spain and hate France and hate Italy," he said. "It's very interesting. Somebody said, ‘They hate their art, they hate the buildings, they hate everything about France. They hate the people. And they let them come in.’" Macron said on Thursday that his government would move to ban protests organized by "individuals or groups with no legitimate authority" as he blamed "ultra-left groups" for the riots and looting that had spread across his country. Trump's comments come after nearly 1,000 people were arrested in France on Saturday as nationwide protests resumed, according to French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez. Violence also erupted in Rome and the Albanian capital of Tirana, where protesters set government buildings ablaze. STATE DEPARTMENT SAYS TRUMP IS 'SPOT ON' WITH FRANCE PROTESTS AFTER MACRON DECRIES 'STUPID' COMMENTS The nationwide marches reflected growing dissatisfaction with the French government, as protesters took to the streets over a range of grievances. The protests began weeks earlier and were led by high school and university students who were frustrated with teacher shortages and poor school conditions. The movement gained momentum when major labor unions joined the demonstrations, expanding the movement to include opposition to government austerity measures and concerns about wages, pensions and the cost of living. PHOTOS SHOW AFTERMATH OF RIOTS AS MASKED GROUPS CLASH WITH POLICE ACROSS FRANCE Asked whether Americans should worry about similar unrest erupting in the United States, Trump pointed to his administration's border security measures. "I think I stopped it. I closed the border. You know that we've had zero infiltration. We've had 0 illegal aliens in the last 18 months. It's almost not believable," he said. The Department of Homeland Security reported a 95% drop in southwest border apprehensions compared to the Biden administration, along with the first fiscal year with zero Border Patrol releases.
