articles.title: Who is Itamar Ben-Gvir, the Israeli firebrand rising with the populist right across the globe?
articles.summary: Itamar Ben-Gvir’s law-and-order agenda has made him one of Israel’s most controversial politicians — and potentially a pivotal player in the country’s next government.
articles.body: Polling ahead of Israel’s Oct. 27 election projects that National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir’s Otzma Yehudit Party will win between seven and ten seats in the 120-member Knesset, potentially making any future government led by Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud Party contingent on his support and positioning him to secure senior ministerial portfolios. His political rise mirrors a broader trend across Europe and the West, where parties such as Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella's National Rally in France, Geert Wilders’ Party for Freedom in the Netherlands, Australia's One Nation leader, Pauline Hanson, Italy’s Matteo Salvini and Germany's Alice Weidel of the AfD have all gained ground on traditional conservative political parties. The highly controversial Ben-Gvir, as national security minister, oversees the ministry responsible for internal security, including the Israel Police, Israel Prison Service and civilian firearms licensing. "I always say that Minister Ben-Gvir, if he were in America, he would just be called a Texan," Yishai Fleisher, international spokesman for the Jewish community of Hebron and a candidate ranked No. 12 on the Otzma Yehudit list, told Fox News Digital. NETANYAHU PRAISES TRUMP'S 'WICKED SENSE OF HUMOR,' DEFENDS IRONCLAD ALLIANCE AHEAD OF HISTORIC ISRAEL VOTE In a video interview with Fox News Digital, Fleisher continued, "Meaning law and order, the death penalty for murderers, tough conditions for jihadists in our prisons and gun rights for the average Jewish person to be able to defend themselves in our national state. That’s what Itamar Ben-Gvir stands for," he added. Fleisher said that mass immigration had fueled Islamist extremism and unrest in parts of Europe, saying Israelis want to avoid similar developments. "There is a jihadist takeover that has come in through immigration, and now the streets of Paris are burning, and the people of Belgium and the U.K. want their countries back," Fleisher said. "In Israel, we don’t want to see Tel Aviv burning," prompting politicians to embrace what are known in the United States as "law-and-order" and "tough-on-crime" candidates. FORMER IDF CHIEF GADI EISENKOT EMERGES AS NETANYAHU’S LEADING ELECTION CHALLENGERFormer Israeli Ambassador to Washington Danny Ayalon said that Ben-Gvir had missed an opportunity to change course despite his lack of military service and past conviction, arguing that his tenure had instead had a damaging impact, including on Israel’s diplomatic standing. "Ben-Gvir spoke in a way that turned the entire world against Israel, portraying it as a racist country by making statements that made Israel a pariah state," Ayalon said. "I always say that Minister Ben-Gvir, if he were in America, he would just be called a Texan...Meaning law and order, the death penalty for murderers. Fleisher praised Ben-Gvir, who he said has cracked down on protection rackets in southern Israel and made significant progress toward what he described as greater equality for Jews on the Temple Mount in Jerusalem, Judaism’s holiest site. "Minister Ben-Gvir was an activist from a very young age. He saw the dangers and evils of the Oslo process with the Palestinians and tried to stop it. He was arrested and stopped many times because of that, and he faced the court many times. It was then-Chief Justice Aharon Barak who once told him, ‘Why don’t you go study to be a lawyer?’" Fleisher said. "Ben-Gvir spoke in a way that turned the entire world against Israel, portraying it as a racist country by making statements that made Israel a pariah state." Ben-Gvir, who studied law, became active in public and political affairs and was first elected to the Knesset in 2021. Following the 2022 elections, he was appointed minister of national security by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. His many critics have taken issue with his firebrand style and what many view as a lack of political correctness. Ambassador Ayalon, a former deputy foreign minister, told Fox News Digital that he also viewed Ben-Gvir’s performance as national security minister negatively. EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT VOTES TO CONFRONT MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD, 'ISLAMIST ENTRYISM' IN OVERWHELMING VOTE "During his tenure, Israel has become less secure internally because crime is rising. Many young people believed in the last election that he would bring governability and authority to areas such as the Negev and the Galilee, on the outskirts of the country, where there is almost no law," Ayalon said. In 2007, Ben-Gvir was convicted of supporting a terrorist organization and inciting racism. His campaign told Fox News Digital that the conviction stemmed from displaying a sticker of the late Rabbi Meir Kahane, whose Kach party was outlawed in 1994, and reflected his support for a Jewish nationalist movement. "As a young man, Minister Ben-Gvir was an intense Jewish nationalist. He has said many times, publicly, that he has matured since then and moved on from those positions." ABBAS DELAYS PALESTINIAN ELECTIONS AGAIN, MAKING MORE THAN TWO DECADES WITHOUT VOTE Recent posts on Ben-Gvir’s social media accounts, along with statements issued through Netanyahu’s and Likud’s official channels, have raised questions about whether the two remain fully aligned. On Oct. 15, Ben-Gvir shared a Hebrew-language media report quoting Netanyahu as saying that he would not serve again as national security minister. In response, Ben-Gvir wrote: "Dear Prime Minister, only the people will decide. Ben Gvir is strong, Israel is strong!" TRUMP SAYS NETANYAHU NEEDS TO BE RE-ELECTED, OR ELSE US WILL HAVE TO 'FINISH THE JOB’ AGAINST IRAN ALONE Last Wednesday, Netanyahu's Likud party appeared to reverse course, posting a message on its official WhatsApp channel stating: "Ben-Gvir is a senior minister in our government, and he will remain so in the next government — provided that the bloc consisting of the Left and Arab parties does not win." Despite the public statements, Ayalon said Netanyahu could opt not to include Ben-Gvir in the next government, even if it meant forming an alliance with opposition parties such as Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar. "Netanyahu is brilliant. He kept Ben-Gvir because it suited him. If he could, he would get rid of him in a minute. Bibi is capable of changing his mind on a dime," Ayalon said. Fleisher credited Ben-Gvir with tripling the number of personal firearms and firearms licenses issued to Israelis over four years, establishing 1,000 rapid-response teams, overhauling the prison system and demolishing 9,000 illegally built homes, particularly in the Negev. In March, the Knesset approved a death-penalty law sponsored by Otzma Yehudit and other lawmakers, a measure Ben-Gvir has strongly championed. "No more hotel-like conditions in our prisons. You’ll know you are being punished for your crime, and these simple policies ultimately deter jihadism," Fleisher told Fox News Digital. Ben-Gvir also represents a strong Jewish identity, strong policies and strong laws to ensure that we don’t lose control of our country," he said. The latest polls show Netanyahu’s bloc slightly behind the opposition, led by Yashar party chief Gadi Eisenkot, but neither side has a clear path to the 61 seats needed for a governing majority.

articles.title: Machado returns to Venezuela after 10 months of exile
articles.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela on Sunday after being in exile for 10 months. “Estoy aquí. Con ustedes,” she wrote Sunday on social platform X, which translates to “I am here. With you.” Machado, the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize recipient, left the country under the protection of a U.S. rescue team…
articles.body:
Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela on Sunday after being in exile for 10 months.

“Estoy aquí. Con ustedes,” she wrote Sunday on social platform X , which translates to “I am here. With you.”

Machado, the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize recipient, left the country under the protection of a U.S. rescue team last December. She worked to certify Venezuela’s 2024 presidential election results to prove that fellow opposition leader Edmundo González won against President Nicolás Maduro amid allegations of widespread election fraud.

Machado went into hiding following the ensuing crackdown and was blocked three times during a 24-hour timeframe in September from reentering Venezuela.

Opposition party Unidad Venezuela praised her return, sharing a photo to social media of Machado embracing tearful supporters as others raised their phones to capture the moment. The party said it was time to unite “toward a democratic, peaceful and orderly transition that allows Venezuelans to fully recover their rights and freely decide their future.”

“Her return must mark a new impetus for the struggle to recover democracy, freedom, and popular sovereignty,” the party wrote on X.

“Today is a very important day for Venezuelans,” González wrote on X . “Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process! Very soon I will be with you and with her so that our country truly advances toward freedom.”

President Trump, who has supported Machado but not her efforts to run for the presidency in her home country, told CNN that he hoped she was safe and was unaware of her return to Venezuela.

“She gave me her Nobel Prize, so how can I say anything else? And I hope she’s safe,” he said.

The opposition leader was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize after Trump vocally campaigned to be nominated for it for his work in ending conflicts around the world. She presented Trump with the award during a visit to the White House in January.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio welcomed Machado’s return, saying it was based on “the U.S. supported reconciliation talks which has already seen hundreds of political prisoners freed and hundreds of political opposition figures return from exile.”

“The United States expects the freedoms of all sectors of Venezuelan politics to continue to be respected,” he wrote on X . “Likewise, we expect all political actors to support these talks which represent the best chance Venezuela has had in thirty years to peacefully achieve not just a free and fair election but an enduring democracy.”

Machado previously vowed that she will run for president if her country holds elections before the end of 2026, after U.S. forces captured Maduro in early January. She told other opposition leaders in Panama that they remain committed to Venezuela’s transition of power and to holding free and fair elections.

The Trump administration has publicly backed ruling-party loyalist and Venezuelan Vice President Delcy Rodríguez as Venezuela’s leader following Maduro’s capture. Machado had worked to win over support from the White House and publicly praised the administration’s intervention in Venezuela.

Trump has said that Machado lacks support among Venezuelans and has praised Rodríguez’s willingness to open Venezuela’s oil industry to foreign investors and pursue closer diplomatic ties with the U.S. amid an energy shortage instigated by the Iran war.

“We thank President Donald Trump, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, the U.S. Government, Congress, and allied governments for their continued leadership and support,” David Smolansky, senior adviser on foreign affairs and security to Machado, said in a statement to The Hill.

“Machado returns to stand with Venezuelans in their pursuit of freedom, democracy, and justice, and to help advance a peaceful, inclusive, and sustainable transition leading to free, fair, and verifiable presidential elections, with guarantees for all,” he added.

articles.title: Parker McCollum wants his sons to learn the lesson hunting and ranch life taught him growing up
articles.summary: Parker McCollum recalls childhood hunting trips with his dad in Texas and reveals how he's passing that same love of the outdoors to his two sons.
articles.body: Parker McCollum has come a long way from the little boy who couldn't wait to tag along on hunting trips with his dad. Now, with two sons of his own, the country music star is looking forward to being on the other side of those childhood memories. And he's already getting a head start. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS McCollum, who welcomed his second son with wife Hallie Ray in July, recently spent several days at the family ranch with his oldest boy, 2-year-old Major. "I was taking him with me to kind of, you know, just do some ranch stuff," McCollum told OutKick OutDoors in an exclusive interview. "He can't really. He just kind of stands out there and pulls grass out of the ground while I'm working or whatever." Major might not be much help around the ranch just yet, but McCollum certainly doesn't mind. After all, he remembers exactly what it was like to be that little boy. Watch Parker McCollum's whole interview with OutKick OutDoors here: "I remember those days so vividly," he said. "My dad would get me out of school early on a Friday to go down to the lease or the ranch or whatever, and we would let it rip all weekend. And a lot of times it was just him and I. "To say that I look forward to doing that for him and with him is an understatement." A lifelong love of hunting Hunting has been part of McCollum's life for as long as he can remember. In a 2022 interview with NRA Country, the Texas native recalled going bird hunting with his father when he was around 8 years old, carrying a single-shot .410 shotgun. He also identified his dad as one of his favorite hunting buddies. But McCollum's love for the outdoors started even before he was old enough to participate. During a 2024 interview with Audacy, McCollum remembered crying when his father and other family members left for hunting trips without him because he was too young to come along. Once he finally got his chance, he was hooked. CHARTER CAPTAIN JONATHAN MOSS EXPLAINS HOW TO GET KIDS HOOKED ON FISHING FROM AN EARLY AGE That outdoors-centered upbringing extended beyond hunting season, too. McCollum spent summers working cattle, branding steers and tending to his grandfather's ranch alongside his cousins. Now he's hoping Major and his younger brother, Rocker, will grow up with that same appreciation for the outdoors. And for McCollum, it's about much more than harvesting deer. 'So good for your soul' With a demanding music career, two young children and a schedule that often keeps him on the road, McCollum understands how difficult it can be to slow down. That's exactly why he believes time outdoors is so important. "There is nothing I love more than sitting in a tree in East Texas or South Texas or the Midwest. Even if you don’t see a dadgum deer," he told OutKick OutDoors. "There's just something about it that's so good for your soul." McCollum explained that his family's trips to the ranch aren’t about checking things off a to-do list or packing as much activity into the day as possible. "Our whole intention was just slowing it down and turning it off and just spending time as a family, and no agenda," he said. "We wake up late and cook breakfast, and hunt in the evenings, and crockpot dinner, and ride around." It's a deliberate departure from the pace of everyday life — one McCollum says is becoming increasingly difficult to escape. And that's precisely the lesson he hopes his sons will carry into adulthood. "Don't ever get so busy or worried about other stuff that you forget to do this." articles.title: NFL fans visiting Paris in high spirits for Saints vs. Steelers game, undeterred by protests
articles.summary: er people.
articles.body: PARIS — American football fans brought high energy, chants and smiles to Stade de France on Sunday to watch the Pittsburgh Steelers face the New Orleans Saints. Some said the mass protests in the city were not an issue during their weekend trip. The NFL’s first regular-season game in France came a day after more than 400,000 people around the country took to the streets to protest educational funding and the high cost of living. At least 110,000 of those protesters were concentrated in Paris, according to the French Interior Ministry. Although the demonstrations were largely peaceful, some clashes broke out, prompting French security forces to use tear gas and water cannons in several cities. Paris prosecutors said there were 64 arrests in the nation’s capital on Saturday, mostly for suspected weapons offenses or participation in a group preparing violence or property damage. But American visitors in town to cheer on their teams told NBC News that everyone they’ve encountered had been welcoming. Lifelong friends and Saints fans Sindhu Pandit, Shruti Menon and Pramod Menon said they never felt the game would be canceled. Pandit said the key to their own movements around the city was to stay informed. “I think we were all given quite a bit of good information from the the different platforms that we were subscribed to,” Pandit said. “And as well as, you know, staying on local news as well — the concierge services at the different hotels were quite good at keeping us informed.” Pramod Menon added that locals were “incredibly hospitable” and considerate of the fact that they were visitors. The friends said they came to support both the country and their team, a sentiment his wife shared. “We’re so excited to be here in Paris, and what a perfect place for for New Orleans, the home of the French,” Shruti Menon said. “And so it’s wonderful to be here.” Sean Warner, a Steelers fan since 1974, may not share the Menons’ taste in teams, but he also told NBC News that he and his wife, Saroja, were having a “wonderful” time in Paris. “We were concerned about the riots and everything that we had heard about and read about, but quite honestly, it’s been amazing,” he said. “The experience has been fantastic. ... Paris has really tried to work hard to, you know, make people feel safe and comfortable, and then enjoy the experience.” The Washington, D.C.-based couple, who have visited Paris several times, spent Saturday walking around the city. Saroja Warner said it was a bit sad to see some businesses with boarded-up windows, but any clashes seemed “localized.” “We walked around Paris all day till about 6 o’clock at night ... and we didn’t see any unrest, any crazy stuff,” she said. “It just felt like a lot of folks trying to have a nice time on a rainy day in Paris.” The Steelers beat the Saints 16-10 at France’s national stadium, just outside the heart of Paris. The game is the latest in a series of international games the NFL has scheduled in recent seasons to grow the sport outside of its domestic audience. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell told reporters Wednesday that he was not concerned about the Paris protests ahead of the game and was comfortable with the security preparations the league had made in coordination with French authorities. “Protests are not unusual in France, as you know, and that’s something that we will be aware of and make sure that the appropriate arrangements are made,” Goodell said. Figures from the Interior Ministry indicate Saturday’s demonstrations produced significantly fewer problems than those the week before. There were about 1,300 arrests nationwide, roughly half the previous week’s total. Only 53 members of the security forces reported injuries, compared with 1,144 the week before, according to the ministry. The unrest began weeks ago, when students at a high school in Créteil, a suburb of Paris, began protesting a lack of resources and poor conditions at their school. Students at other schools in the poorer suburbs surrounding Paris soon joined, and the protests grew into a movement of students across France. The teenagers blocked entrances to their schools and demanded that the French government invest in their educations by increasing staffing, repairing aging buildings and providing more resources to the public education system. Their protests caught the attention of many across the country who were struggling with the high cost of living. Protest organizers agreed to the plans coordinated with the French government on Saturday, the Interior Ministry said Sunday. But the ministry warned that high-risk groups, largely made up “of radical far-left and ultraleft activists,” had infiltrated demonstrations in medium- and large-sized cities. It blamed those groups for “fomenting attacks” against law enforcement, businesses and other people. “While the level of violence from these radical elements was the same as last week, their attempted actions — which triggered systematic intervention by law enforcement in line with the clear instructions of the Minister of the Interior — were generally thwarted,” the ministry said. Richard Engel and Marc Smith reported from Paris. Doha Madani reported from New York City.

articles.title: Uganda orders 21-day Ebola quarantine for citizens returning from DR Congo
articles.summary: Kampala says country is Ebola free, but Swiss authorities believe a woman diagnosed in Nigeria was infected in Uganda.
articles.body:
Uganda has ordered citizens returning after travel to the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) to quarantine for 21 days, as it steps up precautions against the Ebola virus .

Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi announced the measure on Sunday at a news conference in Kampala, as Ebola cases in Kenya and Nigeria raised fresh questions about travellers passing through Uganda.

The country says it has no active infections after ending its own outbreak in July. Returning Ugandans with a history of travel to DRC will have to pay for their quarantine, the Ministry of Health said.

Officials have also strengthened checks at Entebbe International Airport and land crossings, and require all incoming travellers to complete forms recording how they can be contacted.

Uganda declared its Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak over on July 28. It had recorded 20 infections and two deaths, according to the Health Ministry.

Yet Swiss authorities have said a Ugandan-born woman married to a Swiss diplomat contracted Ebola during a visit to Uganda in September.

Nigeria confirmed her infection on October 20, after she had travelled to Abuja, its capital.

At Sunday’s briefing in Kampala, Baryomunsi challenged that conclusion. He said relatives who had previously visited DRC had met the woman in a Kampala suburb, and questioned whether that possible route of exposure had been ruled out.

“We should speak science, not politics,” he said.

The World Health Organization (WHO), the United Nations’ health agency, said on Thursday that the information it had received did not show that the woman herself had travelled to DRC.

Nigerian and Ugandan officials are investigating her movements and possible source of infection.

The inquiry has also turned to a Kenyan man who travelled from DRC through Uganda before flying to Nairobi on October 3. He died two days later, and Kenya has since reported a second Ebola death.

Both patients passed through Entebbe airport on the same day.

Ugandan officials said on Sunday that security footage showed no physical interaction between them.

Nigerian authorities said genetic testing found closely related viruses in the two cases, but no direct link had been established.

Baryomunsi said 60 people traced in Uganda after possible contact with the Kenyan patient had finished 21 days of monitoring and been discharged.

In neighbouring DRC, where the outbreak began in May, the WHO had recorded 9,704 cases and 4,687 deaths by October 20.

Ebola, which can cause haemorrhagic fever, has reached eight Congolese provinces, making this the country’s largest recorded outbreak of the virus. Ebola spreads through direct contact with the bodily fluids of infected people.

The strain responsible for the current outbreak, known as Bundibugyo, has no approved vaccine or specific treatment.

Symptoms can take up to 21 days to appear, according to the WHO. In its October 23 update, the WHO urged stronger monitoring and cooperation across borders, while advising against restrictions on travel or trade with affected countries.

articles.title: Texas student Jose Yepez started a landscaping business to help pay for his college tuition; it into a full outdoor services company and he's now won the National FFA’s 2026 American Star in Agribusiness award
articles.summary: Texas student Jose Yepez won the 2026 American Star in Agribusiness award from the National FFA Organization on Friday.
articles.body: Texas student Jose Yepez won the 2026 American Star in Agribusiness award from the National FFA Organization on Friday. Yepez has been recognised for his landscaping work, which he took on to cover his tuition fees, but his company has since grown to serve more than 100 clients and employ four full-time workers.According to the official release by National FFA Organization, the business has also changed things for his family. Yepez says the money he has earned has helped his mother renovate her home, and his sister attend college. His father has also secured a fulfilling job, while Yepez has managed to pay for his own education. These are the achievements he values most about running his company, Yepez Signature Landscape.Yepez, a member of Greenville FFA in Texas, received the award at the 99th National FFA Convention & Expo in Indianapolis. He was among four students honoured for their work in agriculture-related fields. The winners were announced at Lucas Oil Stadium after a panel of judges interviewed finalists in each category.According to the National FFA Organization, Yepez's company has received more than 160 five-star reviews. Although the business has expanded, he continues to look after much of its daily management. From speaking with customers to handling payments, marketing and work schedules, Yepez remains closely involved in running the company.Life-changing ventureWhen Yepez started Yepez Signature Landscape, his main concern was finding a way to fund his education. The business gave him an opportunity to earn money while building something of his own.As more customers came in, he began offering services beyond basic landscaping. Today, the company takes up landscape design, hardscape construction and property maintenance work. Hardscaping involves building outdoor features using materials such as stone and concrete.With more than 100 clients and four full-time employees, the business has grown considerably from its early days. Yepez now has to manage customer requests, organise work for his employees and keep track of the company's finances.But when asked about what the business has meant to him, Yepez spoke about his family rather than the number of customers or projects.“One of the most impactful opportunities that this project has been able to provide me is the ability to support my family financially,” he said.Yepez explained that his parents are immigrants who have worked hard throughout their lives. Being able to contribute to the family's expenses has therefore been particularly meaningful to him.“As the son of immigrant parents who have known nothing but to work their entire lives tirelessly, I take pride in being able to utilize my business in a meaningful way to assist my family,” he said.The earnings have helped his mother improve her home and his sister pursue higher education. Yepez has also been able to cover his own college costs, fulfilling the goal that first encouraged him to start the business.Why Yepez was chosen for the awardYepez's work earned him the American Star in Agribusiness award, one of the National FFA Organization's highest honours for students involved in agricultural education.The award is not based only on how much a business has grown. Students must also show that they have gained practical experience, developed management skills and met the organisation's educational and leadership requirements.A major part of this process is the Supervised Agricultural Experience (SAE) programme. It allows students to learn through practical work rather than relying entirely on classroom lessons.Some students start and manage their own businesses, while others work for agricultural companies or carry out research projects. These experiences help them apply what they have learnt during their agricultural education.To be considered for an American Star Award, students must first earn the American FFA Degree, the organisation's highest level of student accomplishment.For the 2026 awards, judges interviewed four finalists in each category before selecting the winners. Yepez was chosen in the agribusiness category.Other students who received national honoursThe convention also recognised three students whose agricultural projects took them into different areas of farming and research.Tessa Tauke of Beckman Catholic FFA in Iowa won the American Star in Agriscience award. She began researching problems related to her family's farm while she was still in eighth grade. Her five projects covered subjects such as agricultural equipment safety, black walnut toxicity, welding exposure, and treatments for bovine ringworm.Her research later took her to the US Department of Agriculture, Iowa State University Dairy Farm and the National Mississippi River Museum & Aquarium, where she gained further experience.Jaron Black, from Streator FFA in Illinois, received the American Star in Agricultural Placement award. He started with tasks such as cleaning and moving equipment at Black Farms before taking on more responsibilities. His work eventually included repairing machinery, operating farm vehicles, applying fertilisers and pesticides, and dealing directly with customers.The American Star Farmer award went to Cooper Kline of North Rock Creek FFA in Oklahoma. articles.title: Long queues after power surge at Stansted Airport
articles.summary: A passenger says she was trapped in a corridor at the airport for 90 minutes.
articles.body:
Passengers arriving at Stansted Airport have described waiting in long queues to reach immigration control after a power surge shut down its systems.

Traveller Jill Stakem reported the airport's internal tram system had failed earlier and people were "being held in a corridor for over 90 minutes".

Stakem added: "It's horrendous. No communication, no seating for people, no-one offering watering."

In a statement, a spokesperson for Stansted Airport said: "Due to a power surge earlier today that affected the airport and local area, a number of airport systems were temporarily impacted."

They added: "All systems are now back in service with operational teams working hard to provide support to passengers on their journeys through the airport."

Another airport spokesperson confirmed the shuttle service "remained out-of-service due to a technical fault and contingency bussing is in operation to transfer passengers between the terminal and gates".

The airport apologised "for any disruption and inconvenience they may have experienced while services were being restored".

Stakem said the airport should have better contingency plans in place for such an occurrence.

Gilles Corby, who also contacted the BBC on Sunday afternoon, said: "Queues to passport control extend into the departure terminals.

"It has taken 45 minutes to reach the entrance of the actual immigration queue."

Some trains to and from the airport were cancelled on Saturday after damage was caused to overhead power lines.

Last month hundreds of people were stuck in a corridor in the airport after a shuttle service for arriving passengers ceased operating .

articles.title: Letter making claims about Meghan's father written by his ex-wife, BBC understands
articles.summary: Roslyn Loveless, who has since died, divorced Meghan's father in 1975. Meghan said she had been informed about the "disturbing allegations" in 2018.
articles.body:
A letter sent to the Metropolitan Police making a number of claims relating to the Duchess of Sussex's father was written by his ex-wife Roslyn Loveless, the BBC understands.

Meghan confirmed on Friday she had previously been informed about "disturbing allegations" about her estranged father, Thomas Markle.

On Saturday, the Met confirmed it received a letter relating to Markle in 2019, and it was shared with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex at the time.

It has been reported that images of child sexual abuse allegedly belonging to Markle, 82, had been found in his former home in the Philippines. Markle, who is based in the US, denies all such allegations.

Loveless, who has since died, is the mother of Meghan's half-siblings Samantha Markle and Thomas Markle Jr. Loveless divorced Markle in 1975 before he married the Duchess' mother Doria Ragland in 1979.

Meghan was born in 1981 and is the only daughter of Markle and Ragland.

In a statement shared on Friday, Meghan confirmed the existence of the letter and wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."

She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".

Meghan has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls.

Sources close to the duchess said Meghan warned Markle in a letter - sent while he was in hospital in the Philippines after having his leg amputated - that he would never meet his grandchildren.

On Friday, Meghan's half-brother claimed to the Sun he found a stash of images belonging to his father at his former Philippines home.

He is reported to have told police he discovered child abuse videos and pictures among the items.

He also apologised to Meghan for initially siding with her father during their long-running estrangement, and said he had "been protecting the wrong person for the past nine years".

It is understood that he contacted the US Federal Bureau of Investigations (FBI) about the images in July. The FBI has since confirmed it is aware of the allegations.

Officials in the Philippines have confirmed they are investigating allegations relating to Markle.

They told the BBC on Friday that the Philippines' anti-human trafficking and child sexual exploitation task force was investigating the matter.

Markle gave an interview to the Mail on Sunday in which he acknowledged paying for sex in the Philippines on past visits but denied sleeping with underage girls and ever possessing child abuse images.

The Met Police has said it did not pass on the contents of the letter shared with the Sussexes to other law enforcement agencies. The force is now reviewing its handling of the matter.

Markle moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes.

He is reportedly now living in a Florida rehabilitation centre learning to walk again after having his leg amputated.

articles.title: Buccaneers collect two freakish first-half scores to dominate Panthers – and, oh, Baker Mayfield is back
articles.summary: Calijah Kancey's 32-yard fumble return and Zyon McCollum's blocked extra point conversion powers the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' dominant first half.
articles.body: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are scoring points in the most unorthodox ways against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. The Bucs led the Panthers convincingly with a 33-6 lead at halftime and 8 of their points came in freakish fashion. The freakish fashion? A defensive two-point conversion by cornerback Zyon McCullom. A big-man touchdown fumble return by 280-pound defensive tackle Calijah Kancey. Not typical. BAKER MAYFIELD LEAVES GAME AFTER WRITHING IN PAIN ON TURF IN TAMPA BAY WHEN THUMB ON THROWING HAND INJURED Let's begin with the Kancey score first. The Bucs have so far smothered the Panthers' offense and evidence of that was Al-Quadin Muhammad's strip-sack of Carolina quarterback Bryce Young. articles.title: Give mayors real powers, ensure timely civic audits, urban body heads tell Centre
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Even as the Centre moots directly elected mayors with a fixed five-year tenure and a mayor-in-council system, municipal heads from different
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Even as the Centre moots directly elected mayors with a fixed five-year tenure and a mayor-in-council system, municipal heads from different cities at National Urban Conclave flagged that the move would serve little purpose without giving mayors adequate powers. Rajkot mayor Nehal Shukla also called for time-bound financial audits of civic bodies, saying that “no municipal body can function without financial irregularities”.Participating in a discussion on proposed changes to the Model Municipal Law, Shukla said mayors in municipal governance were like governors, while standing committees wielded financial powers and executive officials remained under the control of state govts.“Wherever we have directly elected mayors, we must have a mayor-in-council. If you don’t give power to the mayor, direct election hardly serves any objective,” he said.Under the mayor-in-Council system, executive powers to run a city on a day-to-day basis are shared between the mayor and a small, cabinet-like group of elected councillors, who are individually accountable for their respective portfolios.Shukla also suggested that municipal elections be conducted by the Election Commission, citing its track record of holding timely general and assembly elections. He said state govts invariably found one reason or another to delay municipal polls.“The biggest missing thing that needs to be fixed is timely audits to bring financial discipline. Audit reports are delayed by six to eight years, and that’s why irregularities do not come to light. We all know that no municipal body can function without financial irregularities,” he said.Shukla pointed out that rules require tenders to be floated for works or services costing more than Rs 5 lakh, but alleged that this was often not followed. Municipal commissioners, he said, were aware of such violations but approved the transactions because otherwise civic bodies could not function.He suggested that audits be conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG). If state auditors continued to conduct them, he said, the law should ensure that the audit backlog did not exceed two years.Bhubaneswar mayor Sulochana Das, who also participated in the discussion, said municipal laws were robust on paper, but the ground reality was different.“People have more expectations from directly elected mayors. But we have no power. Executive officers such as municipal commissioners are beyond the control of mayors, as we cannot write their annual performance reports or have any say in their appointments. Commissioners change frequently,” she said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Elvis Presley’s rights holders sue Anthropic saying it trained AI on his music
articles.summary: The owners of Elvis Presley’s music have sued Anthropic for allegedly using his copyrighted lyrics without permission to train its AI models and generating infringing versions of his songs.
articles.body: The owners of Elvis Presley’s music have sued Anthropic for allegedly using his copyrighted lyrics without permission to train its AI models and generating infringing versions of his songs. In a lawsuit filed Friday, Authentic Brands Group, the licensing platform that controls Presley’s intellectual property — along with other companies, trusts and individuals who own rights to his music — accused Anthropic of infringing copyrights to 274 songs without any license or payment. These span some of Presley’s biggest hits, including “All Shook Up,” “Can’t Help Falling in Love,” “Don’t Be Cruel,” “A Little Less Conversation” and “Return to Sender.” “The Elvis Plaintiffs’ iconic collective catalog contains some of the most groundbreaking, revolutionary, influential, and enduring musical compositions in human history,” the lawsuit stated. The plaintiffs allege that the infringement has occurred throughout “the entire development” of Anthropic’s flagship Claude models and continues today as users generate outputs that reproduce copyrighted lyrics or create unauthorized adaptations of the songs. “As we say in the lawsuit, the Elvis Plaintiffs are guardians of, and highly protective of, Elvis’s song which are some of the most iconic of all time,” attorney Richard Busch wrote in a statement. A spokesperson for Anthropic wrote: “We disagree with the claims and intend to defend this case fully.” The complaint further describes Anthropic as having “built its entire business model on infringing copyrights at an unfathomable scale,” pointing to the alleged mass scraping of internet content and pirating of books to develop its Claude language models. Last year, Anthropic agreed to a landmark $1.5 billion settlement in a copyright infringement lawsuit filed by authors who alleged the company had illegally used pirated copies of their books to train AI models. It was the largest settlement in the history of American copyright cases. The lawsuit by Presley’s rights holders comes amid a larger wave of lawsuits against Anthropic and other AI companies for allegedly using copyrighted musical works without consent or compensation. In January, Universal Music, Concord Music Group and ABKCO Music expanded their lawsuit against Anthropic over the alleged infringement of copyrighted song lyrics. BMG Rights Management, Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Music filed similar lawsuits against Anthropic this year. Anthropic and the AI music generation company Suno were also recently hit with lawsuits from the independent music publisher Round Hill — which is represented by Busch, the lead attorney for Presley’s rights holders — and the independent music company Reservoir Media. “Even after the Defendant supposedly put up ‘guardrails’ after being sued, in one of its latest iterations, Claude continues to infringe,” the Presley rights holders state in their lawsuit. The complaint notes that when asked recently to re-create specific songs “for a modern audience,” Claude did so. “These renders keep landing very close to the originals: same structure, same hooks reused with light rewording, and full sets of verses/choruses/bridges,” the complaint said. “That’s edging past ‘inspired by’ into reproducing the copyrighted song, even when the words are swapped out.” Presley’s rights holders are seeking $41.1 million in statutory copyright damages — up to $150,000 for each of the 274 works they alleged were willfully infringed — according to the complaint. They also demand a permanent injunction to prevent Anthropic from “further infringing” on Presley’s works and an order for the company to destroy all unauthorized copies of the copyrighted works.

articles.title: Serbia voter turnout highest in decades as students oppose longtime leader
articles.summary: Election commission says turnout reaches 65% amid allegations of intimidation, violence and voting irregularities.
articles.body:
Polls have closed in Serbia’s snap parliamentary election , which saw the highest voter turnout in decades, with a student-backed movement seeking to unseat longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic.

Voting ended at 8pm local time (19:00 GMT) on Sunday, with first indications of the result expected a few hours later.

The vote will determine whether Vucic’s Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), which has governed since 2012, can retain power against a movement born from nationwide anticorruption protests .

The State Election Commission said that voter turnout had reached 64.9 percent by 17:00GMT, ⁠⁠the ⁠⁠highest since ⁠⁠the breakup ‌‌of Yugoslavia in ‌‌1992.

The higher turnout does not show which side gained support.

University of Belgrade researcher Jelena Vasiljevic told Al Jazeera in an interview published on Friday that the SNS had a reliable voter base, while the students needed to attract people who normally did not vote.

Sunday’s voting was also marked by reports of intimidation and procedural problems.

The Centre for Research, Transparency and Accountability (CRTA), an independent election watchdog, said its observers recorded pressure on voters or election workers at almost a third of the 500 polling stations it monitored.

It also reported failures to protect ballot secrecy.

By 5pm (16:00 GMT), the Centre for Free Elections and Democracy (CeSID), an election-monitoring group, had received about 260 reports of potential irregularities, including ballot photography, group voting and difficulties with identification checks.

In Belgrade, police wearing riot helmets and carrying shields deployed near the election commission’s headquarters, where roads were closed and barricades erected.

City prosecutors appealed on Sunday for everyone involved in the election to avoid violence.

The election follows nearly two years of student-led protests that began after a railway station canopy collapsed in Novi Sad in November 2024, killing 16 people.

Demands for accountability widened into a movement against alleged government corruption and repression. Vucic and the SNS deny those accusations.

The Student List – Students Win, which emerged from demonstrations, is fielding candidates drawn from professions, including medicine and education, many of whom have no political experience.

The movement campaigns for stronger institutions and an end to corruption.

Some established opposition parties have backed the students rather than field candidates of their own.

Vucic resigned as president in September to run for prime minister, promising higher pensions, public-sector wages and investment.

Supporters credit his rule with modernising Serbia’s economy.

About six and a half million people were eligible to vote for 250 parliamentary seats, with 18 electoral lists competing. A majority of 126 seats is needed to form a government.

articles.title: After their granddaughter needed intensive care at birth, a New York couple's foundation pledged $10 million to expand a neonatal unit; the gift will match community donations and support care for hundreds of babies
articles.summary: A New York couple whose granddaughter needed intensive care after birth is helping fund expanded medical care for newborns through a $10 million
articles.body: A New York couple whose granddaughter needed intensive care after birth is helping fund expanded medical care for newborns through a $10 million philanthropic commitment. According to Catholic Health’s official announcement, the $10 million matching commitment from the Donald and Barbara Zucker Family Foundation is the largest philanthropic gift in the history of Good Samaritan University Hospital in West Islip, Long Island. The funding will support the transformation and expansion of the hospital’s neonatal intensive care unit (NICU), where critically ill and premature babies receive specialised treatment. The commitment will also match eligible community donations, encouraging more families and supporters to contribute to the project.A family’s experience inspires a major giftThe donation comes from the Donald and Barbara Zucker Family Foundation. Barbara Hrbek Zucker explained that her family experienced the need for specialised neonatal care when their youngest granddaughter was born and required intensive medical support. According to Catholic Health, the granddaughter received the care she needed and is now thriving. Barbara Hrbek Zucker said the family wanted to help ensure that other families could access specialised neonatal care close to home.The contribution is significant not only because of its size but also because it comes from a family that has personally experienced the uncertainty surrounding a newborn’s health. The foundation’s support is intended to help other families navigate similar circumstances with access to specialised medical teams and a more supportive hospital environment.How the $10 million matching commitment will workThe foundation’s commitment is structured as a matching gift, meaning qualifying community donations will be matched dollar for dollar under the programme’s terms. Catholic Health is seeking the first $2.5 million in qualifying community commitments by the end of 2026, as part of a four-year effort to secure $10 million in community support. This approach is designed to encourage broader participation in the project. Rather than relying on a single philanthropic contribution, the hospital hopes to involve individuals, families and other donors in financing the NICU’s transformation.The matching arrangement can increase the impact of eligible donations while giving community members a direct way to support neonatal care. The overall fundraising effort will help advance the hospital’s plans to modernise the unit and provide resources for vulnerable newborns and their families.What the upgraded neonatal unit will offerThe planned expansion and modernisation will introduce advanced medical equipment and technology, private patient rooms, and dedicated areas for family counselling, respite and support. A neonatal intensive care unit provides specialised treatment for newborns who need close monitoring or advanced medical intervention, including premature babies and infants with complex health conditions. Such care can require specialised equipment, continuous observation and coordinated work by doctors, nurses and other clinical professionals.The hospital intends to create an environment that supports both clinical needs and the emotional demands experienced by families. Private rooms can offer greater privacy during difficult periods, while designated counselling and respite areas can give parents space to receive guidance, rest and discuss their child’s care with medical teams. Justin Lundbye, president of Good Samaritan University Hospital, said the project would provide greater comfort and privacy for families while giving clinical teams an environment better suited to the care they deliver.A regional centre for high-risk newborn careGood Samaritan University Hospital, located in West Islip, is home to the only Level III NICU on the South Shore of Suffolk County, according to Catholic Health. It serves as an important regional destination for women experiencing high-risk pregnancies and families whose newborns need specialised care. The hospital delivered more than 2,500 babies in 2025, while its NICU treats hundreds of newborns each year. The planned improvements are intended to strengthen this service and help the hospital respond to the needs of families across the surrounding communities.The project also reflects the importance of having specialised neonatal services available close to home. When a baby needs intensive care, families may face extended hospital stays, uncertainty and significant emotional pressure. Access to experienced clinical teams and suitable facilities can help support babies while giving parents opportunities to remain involved in their care. The foundation’s gift will support the hospital’s effort to improve these services, while the matching campaign offers the wider community an opportunity to contribute to the project.Investing in the future of neonatal careThe $10 million commitment marks a milestone in Good Samaritan University Hospital’s philanthropic history and gives its neonatal care expansion a substantial funding boost. It also demonstrates how personal experiences can motivate long-term investment in healthcare services that benefit other families.For the Zucker family, the gift is rooted in gratitude for the specialised care their granddaughter received. For the hospital, it represents an opportunity to modernise its NICU, strengthen family support and continue caring for vulnerable newborns across Long Island. With additional community donations expected to be matched through the programme, the initiative aims to turn one family’s experience into a wider investment in neonatal care.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘I am here. With you’: Nobel laureate, Venezuela opposition leader Machado returns after nearly a year in exile
articles.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela on Sunday after nearly a year in exile.
articles.body: Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela on Sunday after nearly a year in exile. Her team confirmed her return, in a move likely to increase pressure on interim president Delcy Rodríguez as the country’s political future remains uncertain.“I am here. With you,” Machado wrote in Spanish on X, without disclosing how she had re-entered the country or providing details of her whereabouts.Her close ally, exiled opposition leader Edmundo González Urrutia, also confirmed her return in a social media post. “Venezuela! I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear María Corina, is on Venezuelan soil,” he wrote, adding that he would return soon.Machado was later seen at a church in Barquisimeto, the capital of Lara state, about 220 miles west of Caracas. Footage and photographs published by news organisations showed supporters greeting and embracing her during a religious ceremony at the Sanctuary of the Divine Shepherdess.Machado’s exileMachado left Venezuela covertly in December 2025 to receive the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway. Since then, she has made several attempts to return, but Venezuelan authorities blocked her entry, according to her party and her advisers. Her return comes amid continuing uncertainty over the country’s political transition following the removal of former president Nicolás Maduro by US forces in January.Machado’s opposition movement is widely believed to have won the 2024 presidential election, although Maduro was declared the winner and refused to hand over power. González, who stood in the election after Machado was barred from running, has been living in exile.Following Maduro’s ouster, Rodríguez, his former vice-president, assumed the role of interim president with the backing of US president Donald Trump’s administration. Washington has prioritised economic stabilisation and access to Venezuela’s oil, while Machado and her allies have pressed for a date for fresh presidential elections.The Guardian reported that the Trump administration had opposed Machado’s return, fearing it could complicate its relationship with Rodríguez. However, Trump told reporters on Sunday that he did not know about Machado’s return, adding that he hoped she was safe. “She’s a very nice woman,” he said, referring to the Nobel Peace Prize medal Machado had given him.US secretary of state Marco Rubio said the circumstances that enabled Machado’s return were the result of US support for reconciliation talks. In a post on X, Rubio said Washington expected the freedoms of all sectors of Venezuelan politics to be respected and urged political actors to support negotiations aimed at achieving free and fair elections.Machado’s homecoming comes as her party continues to demand an electoral timetable. Rodríguez’s interim administration has held rounds of negotiations with a section of the opposition and agreed to judicial reforms, but no date for a presidential election has been announced.Machado has repeatedly praised Trump for the operation that removed Maduro and presented him with her Nobel medal during a meeting in January. Her return now puts renewed focus on whether Venezuela’s political transition will lead to competitive elections and what role the opposition will play in shaping the country’s future.You use AI every day. articles.summary: In March 2023, professional golfer Sergio Garcia and his wife Angela raised $2 million for children’s healthcare and foster care through the inaugural FORE Kids ATX fundraiser in Austin, Texas. The event featured a golf tournament, a charity gala, and entertainment from notable figures, benefitting multiple organizations supporting youth programs.
articles.body: Professional golfer Sergio Garcia and his wife, Angela, raised $2 million through the first FORE Kids ATX fundraiser in Austin, Texas, in March 2023. The two-day event combined a golf tournament, a charity gala and appearances by professional golfers and entertainers, with proceeds supporting organisations working in children’s healthcare, foster care and youth golf programmes.The fundraiser brought together golfers including Dustin Johnson, Bryson DeChambeau and Brooks Koepka. LIV Golf analyst David Feherty hosted the gala, while country singer Chris Lane performed. FORE Kids ATX reported the $2 million total in its account of the event,Four organisations shared the event’s focusThe inaugural fundraiser partnered with Dell Children’s Medical Center, Foster Village and The Muny Conservancy’s Austin Golf Academy, and the Garcias’ own UGLI Foundation was also among the organisations that were supported by their broader charitable work. Dell Children’s Medical Center provides specialised paediatric healthcare in Central Texas, and Foster Village supports children and families involved in the foster care system, while the Austin Golf Academy works to expand access to golf and youth programming. The UGLI Foundation, founded by Angela Garcia, focuses on bullying prevention and promoting respect for people who may be treated differently because of their appearance or identity.The event’s mix of beneficiaries meant that the proceeds were not restricted to a single medical cause; instead, the fundraiser supported programmes spanning healthcare, family services, youth development and anti-bullying work. The University of Texas alumni publication The Alcalde reported that the Garcias returned with a second annual FORE Kids ATX fundraiser in 2023, and that the two-day event included a golf tournament featuring 120 professional golfers and raised money for Dell Children’s Medical Center, Foster Village, The Muny Conservancy and the UGLI Foundation.Golf provided the centrepieceFORE Kids ATX was built around a multi-day format rather than a single dinner or auction, and golf gave professional players and other guests a way to participate directly, while the evening gala brought donors and supporters together away from the course. Garcia, a Masters champion, has a long record of charitable work through golf, and his foundation, established in 2002, has supported children and young people through social assistance and sports programmes. The Sergio and Angela Garcia Foundation also backs initiatives in the Austin area, where the couple lives, and the couple’s official foundation website identifies Dell Children’s Medical Center, Foster Village, the Austin youth golf programme and the UGLI Foundation as beneficiaries of FORE Kids ATX. It also describes the event as part of their wider work supporting children and families.A recurring fundraiser in AustinThe 2023 event was the first FORE Kids ATX fundraiser hosted by Sergio and Angela Garcia, and its $2 million result gave the organisers a substantial fundraising base for their work with local organisations. The event also relied on the involvement of professional golfers and public figures, whose participation helped attract attention and donors.FORE Kids ATX has since continued to develop as a multi-day fundraiser, with golf, a gala and additional activities built around its charitable partners. The original $2 million figure refers to the 2023 event, not the couple’s total lifetime charitable giving, and their broader foundation work extends beyond FORE Kids ATX and includes other programmes and partnerships.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2025, Pope Leo XIV’s childhood home faced auction; his Illinois hometown bought it for $375,000 and plans to preserve it as a historic site
articles.summary: In a significant turn of events, Dolton, Illinois has purchased Pope Leo XIV’s childhood home for $375,000 to preserve it as a historic site, attracting national interest following the pope's election. The village aims to develop the site for public use and tourism, amid financial challenges.
articles.body: Pope Leo XIV’s childhood home was heading toward auction in 2025 when the village stepped in and purchased the property for $375,000. The small brick house in Dolton, Illinois, had attracted visitors after Robert Francis Prevost became the first U.S.-born pope in May. By December, Dolton had designated the home an official historic landmark, with plans to pursue funding for its preservation and possible public use.The village completed the purchase on July 8, 2025, after negotiations with the previous owner, with the two-story residence at 212 East 141st Place being placed on the market before Prevost’s election, but the sale plans changed after its connection to the new pope became widely known.The house became a destination after the papal electionPrevost was born in Chicago in 1955 and grew up in Dolton, a suburb about 20 miles south of the city. His parents bought the house in 1949, and the family lived there until 1969, when he left to attend seminary school in Michigan. Before his election as pope, Prevost had spent decades working as a priest and missionary, including many years in Peru. His election on May 8, 2025, brought national and international attention to the neighbourhood where he grew up, and visitors began travelling to the property, with some treating it as a place of pilgrimage. The house itself was a modest family residence rather than a church or a building designed for public visits.The Associated Press reported in July that the sudden interest had created an opportunity for Dolton to attract visitors, but the purchase also raised questions about public spending. The village had been dealing with serious financial difficulties, including a reported $3.65 million in debt and unpaid bills. Some residents questioned whether local taxpayers could afford both the purchase and the cost of maintaining the property.Why Dolton chose to buy the propertyVillage leaders considered the home to be a potential asset for tourism and community development, and before reaching a purchase agreement, officials had discussed using eminent domain, a legal process that allows a government to acquire private property for public use. The village ultimately bought the house through a negotiated sale rather than taking it through that process.The purchase price included applicable real estate and auction fees, according to reporting by OSV News. The property had previously been listed for sale and was later put up for auction through Paramount Realty USA, and its former owner had renovated the house before the pope’s election, with a construction company also providing a new roof at no charge. Officials discussed working with the Archdiocese of Chicago and seeking public or private funding to support the property’s future use. Ideas included opening it to visitors and developing a site connected to the pope’s early life.The home received historic landmark status in DecemberThe village took a formal step toward preservation on December 1, 2025, when its Board of Trustees voted unanimously to designate the house an official historic landmark. CBS Chicago reported that the designation would allow Dolton to seek state funding for preservation and development, and officials also discussed the possibility of creating a museum in partnership with the Archdiocese of Chicago.The designation did not mean that the home had already become a public museum or that a full restoration had been completed, since the village still needed to organise funding, management and plans for the site. Mayor Jason House said officials were targeting spring 2027 for completion of the broader project, although that remained a target rather than a confirmed opening date. The next stage involves deciding how the property will be maintained and what visitors will be able to see there. The house is now municipally owned and formally recognised as a historic site, but its long-term use will depend on the funding and plans the village develops.You use AI every day. articles.title: A New York homeowner signed a mortgage in 2005 and later faced foreclosure; after a bank won a ruling, an appeals court reversed it because the lender had not proved it could enforce the note
articles.summary: A New York man who took out a mortgage in 2005 has managed to overturn a court ruling that had gone in favour of a bank seeking to foreclose on his
articles.body: A New York man who took out a mortgage in 2005 has managed to overturn a court ruling that had gone in favour of a bank seeking to foreclose on his property. The US Bank National Association had accused Moses Sukljian of failing to make his loan payments and secured a favourable ruling in 2025. However, on Friday, a state appeals court reversed the decision after finding that the bank had not provided enough evidence to prove it had the legal right to enforce the loan.According to the ruling published by the New York State Unified Court System, the bank had failed to provide sufficient proof concerning documents used to transfer the right to enforce the loan. As a result, the earlier judgment in the bank's favour could not stand.The 2005 mortgage and foreclosure disputeThe story began in December 2005, when Sukljian signed a mortgage agreement with WMC Mortgage Corp. for a property in Albany County, New York. Along with the mortgage, he signed a promissory note, a document recording his promise to repay the borrowed money.Over time, the loan was transferred to another company. By 2018, Ocwen Loan Servicing, LLC, was handling it, and Sukljian entered into an agreement that changed the original repayment terms.The revised arrangement increased the principal balance of the loan and fixed a new monthly payment. A year later, Ocwen merged with PHH Mortgage Corporation, which continued servicing the mortgage.The matter reached court in July 2023, when US Bank National Association filed a foreclosure lawsuit. It claimed Sukljian had defaulted on the loan and sought permission to proceed with the case.The bank supported its claim with the mortgage papers, the 2018 modification agreement, payment records, and a notice about missed instalments. It also asked for an official to be appointed to calculate the amount outstanding.In July 2025, the lower court accepted the bank's position. It ruled that the documents were sufficient, removed Sukljian's defence and directed that the outstanding debt be calculated. Sukljian, however, appealed, arguing that the bank had not proved its right to enforce the original loan.Bank documents became deciding factorThe appeals court had to examine whether US Bank National Association was legally entitled to bring the foreclosure case in the first place.The difficulty arose because Sukljian had signed the original promissory note in favour of WMC Mortgage Corp., while the foreclosure case had been filed by US Bank National Association years later.For a bank to enforce such a loan, it must establish that the right to do so was properly transferred to it. One way of demonstrating this is through an endorsement on the promissory note.An endorsement can also appear on a separate document called an allonge. This is an additional sheet that must be firmly attached to the original note and can be used to record the transfer of enforcement rights.When the bank first filed its lawsuit, the copy of the promissory note it submitted did not contain an endorsement establishing its right to enforce the loan. There was also no accompanying allonge containing the necessary endorsement.The bank subsequently produced two allonges, one of which identified it as the party entitled to payment. But both documents were undated, and neither had been included with the original complaint.This left the court unable to establish whether the documents had been properly attached to the note when the foreclosure proceedings began.What the appeals court foundThe bank had also relied on a statement from a senior loan analyst at PHH Mortgage Corporation. The analyst confirmed that PHH had obtained the original promissory note before the lawsuit was filed.However, the statement did not say whether the allonges were attached to the note at that time. It also did not establish when the documents were created or when they came into the bank's possession.These missing details mattered because the bank needed to prove that it had the right to enforce the loan in July 2023, not merely at some later stage.The appeals court therefore concluded that the bank had not established its legal standing sufficiently to obtain judgment in its favour without a trial.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2018, U.S. soccer star Julie Ertz and NFL tight end Zach Ertz raised $200,000 at their first gala; $80,000 funded scholarships for Haitian students and $50,000 backed college readiness
articles.summary: In 2018, U.S. soccer star Julie Ertz and NFL tight end Zach Ertz raised $200,000 at their inaugural gala for the Ertz Family Foundation, funding scholarships in Haiti and college readiness programs in California while supporting youth sports and education.
articles.body: U.S. soccer player Julie Ertz and Philadelphia Eagles tight end Zach Ertz raised $200,000 at the first gala for their family foundation in July 2018. $80,000 of that amount funded college scholarships for orphaned high school graduates in Haiti, while another $50,000 supported a college-readiness programme for first-generation students in Richmond, California. The remaining proceeds supported the foundation’s wider work in youth sports, education and family services.The couple established the Ertz Family Foundation in the summer of 2018 after Zach visited Haiti with teammates and Mission of Hope, an organisation working with local communities. The trip helped shape the foundation’s focus on education and access to sports, and a November 2018 report by the Philadelphia Eagles detailed the first gala’s fundraising total and how the money was allocated.Scholarships for students in HaitiThe $80,000 contribution went to Mission of Hope Haiti to establish a scholarship programme for more than a dozen students who had graduated from high school after growing up in an orphanage, and was intended to cover college expenses, including tuition, room and board, meals and learning materials. The programme addressed a specific barrier for students who had completed secondary education but lacked the financial resources to continue. The Ertz family’s donation was earmarked for scholarships that would support students through college.The National Football League Players Association also reported the scholarship donation when Zach Ertz was named its Week 5 Community MVP in October 2018, and the union said the $80,000 gift would provide full scholarships for orphaned high school graduates in Haiti. Zach’s visit to Haiti earlier that year had included volunteering in communities where children had limited access to sports equipment and facilities, and he returned with a stronger interest in supporting projects that combined education, sports and community resources. articles.title: Rain cleans up NCR air, but AQI set to be ‘poor’ again today
articles.summary: Rain and gusty winds briefly improved AQI in Noida, Ghaziabad and Greater Noida, but IMD forecasts ‘poor’ air again as dust, construction and weak winds return.
articles.body: Noida: Rain and gusty winds pushed Ghaziabad, Noida and Greater Noida into the ‘moderate’ air quality category on Sunday, but the respite is likely to last just a day. All three cities are likely to slide back into the ‘poor’ category from Monday as pollution levels rise again.According to Central Pollution Control Board’s (CPCB) 4pm bulletin, Ghaziabad recorded an AQI of 125, sharply down from 217 on Saturday. Noida’s AQI fell to 131 from 171, while Greater Noida recorded 134 against 169 a day earlier.The improvement followed a spell of rain and strong winds triggered by a western disturbance on Saturday night. Rain can wash some airborne particles out of the atmosphere, while stronger winds disperse pollutants. However, the effect may not last once conditions turn less favourable.The air quality forecast bulletin of India Meteorological Department’s Environment Monitoring and Research Centre (EMRC) has predicted ‘poor’ air across NCR cities over the next three days. Cooler nights, weaker winds at certain times and a more stable atmosphere could allow pollutants to accumulate instead of dispersing.The nature of pollution also varies across the region. PM10, which includes coarse dust particles, was the main contributor in Greater Noida. In Noida and Ghaziabad, finer PM2.5 particles were also prominent, raising concerns over emissions from several sources.Local environmentalist Amit Gupta said poorly managed construction and road dust were major pollution sources in central Noida. “Industries on the periphery may contribute to PM2.5 levels, but we face dust every day while commuting on the roads,” he added.Residents of Sector 150 have also protested against uncovered trucks transporting soil and construction material through residential areas. Aman Nijhawan, a resident, said builders appeared to be speeding up work ahead of possible Stage III restrictions under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), when construction activity could face tighter curbs.“To speed up work, trucks carrying construction material take routes through residential areas, adding to the misery of residents,” he said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Noida | Silver Rate in Noida | Bank Holidays in Noida | Public Holidays in Noida | Noida AQI | Weather in Noida | Petrol Price in Noida | Diesel Price in Noida | CNG Price in Noida | LPG Price in NoidaStay updated with the latest Noida news. articles.title: Upkeep agency blocks deliveries, house helps at condominium in Greater Noida West over dues
articles.summary: Residents of Ajnara Homes, Greater Noida West, protest as builder’s maintenance agency blocks deliveries and domestic help over 4 months’ dues amid upkeep complaints.
articles.body: Noida: Residents who withheld four months’ maintenance fee over alleged poor upkeep at Ajnara Homes were left scrambling for food and essentials on Sunday after the builder’s maintenance agency allegedly barred delivery agents and domestic help from entering the condominium in Greater Noida West.The move triggered a fresh confrontation at the 15-tower complex, which is home to 2,600 flats and around 10,000 residents. Flat owners said they had little choice but to withhold the fee because complaints about falling plaster, malfunctioning lifts and unhygienic basements had gone unresolved. They said they would resume payments only if amenities were made available.Some residents staged a protest at the society’s main gate after the services were stopped.On Oct 10, TOI reported that residents had been trapped in malfunctioning lifts on three occasions in a week. Repeated calls and messages to the agency seeking a comment went unanswered on Sunday.Omkar Nirala, a resident of Tower C, said his order for milk and bread was stopped at the gate on Sunday morning. “I had to walk around 800 metres from my tower to the gate to collect my delivery. I was waiting for tea, and my family wanted breakfast. But the maintenance staff did not listen to our pleas. They said services were being denied because we had stopped paying maintenance,” he told TOI.Residents said delivery personnel from Amazon, Blinkit and Flipkart were turned away, forcing people to collect groceries and medicines at the main gate.“How can they expect women and the elderly to walk to the gate for groceries or medicines?” asked Chandan Sinha, president of apartment owners’ association (AOA). He said residents had been demanding a handover of maintenance to the AOA because the agency’s agreement had expired more than four years ago.Dinkar Pandey, another resident, alleged that the agency staff had also stopped garbage collection and turned away guests and service providers. “This has been happening intermittently for nearly a month. Today, it led to a confrontation,” he said.Later in the day, AOA members and residents met the Bisrakh SHO, who assured them he would take up the matter with the builder’s staff.Pandey said the agency had often cited financial constraints to explain the poor upkeep, but residents were not convinced. He also questioned the way residents were being billed, and alleged that sewage treatment plant breakdowns, waste management problems and inadequate security at the society were common.Sunday’s dispute raises fresh questions about the agency’s authority to restrict access over unpaid dues.Section 22 of the UP Apartment Act allows an AOA’s general body to curtail an essential service for unpaid common expenses only after dues have remained unpaid for more than six months. This includes at least seven days’ notice, a general-body resolution, and sending a certified copy to the owner and competent authority. Action can follow only after a month has elapsed and the resolution has been displayed publicly. The law does not specifically mention food deliveries or domestic help.But at Ajnara Homes, residents said dues had been withheld for four months, and the restriction was imposed by the builder’s maintenance agency, not through the AOA.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Noida | Silver Rate in Noida | Bank Holidays in Noida | Public Holidays in Noida | Noida AQI | Weather in Noida | Petrol Price in Noida | Diesel Price in Noida | CNG Price in Noida | LPG Price in NoidaStay updated with the latest Noida news.
